codeMaps.summary:
All paths are under /home/user/Zeeba. Read-only investigation; nothing was built or run. Items marked "Recommendation" are my inference, everything else is read directly from the cited lines.

OVERVIEW
A label is a plain string stored in outfits.labels text[] (default '{}', NOT NULL, no check constraint: supabase/migrations/20260101000000_baseline_schema.sql:182). The only source of the selectable list is the const OUTFIT_LABELS (src/services/dataService.types.ts:215-226, 10 values) and its union type OutfitLabel (:228). A label is written exactly once, at outfit creation (single-select, wrapped into a one-element array), and read back in exactly one place: the filter pills on the Outfits grid. Labels are never displayed on the outfit detail page and cannot be edited afterwards.

(1) EVERY READER OF OUTFIT_LABELS / OutfitLabel / outfit.labels
- src/services/dataService.types.ts:199 Outfit.labels: string[] - already a runtime string array, no change.
- dataService.types.ts:210-226 OUTFIT_LABELS const, :228 OutfitLabel type, :240 NewOutfitInput.label: OutfitLabel (JSDoc :230-234 says label is required). Needs: keep the const as the default/seed list (e.g. DEFAULT_OUTFIT_LABELS), make label a string (or string | null if a closet may have zero labels).
- src/components/OutfitsGrid.tsx:7,10 (imports), :29 selectedLabel state typed OutfitLabel | null, :72 filter `outfit.labels.includes(selectedLabel)` (exact, case-sensitive match), :81 `<FilterPills options={OUTFIT_LABELS} ...>`. Needs: options from the active closet's list; selectedLabel as string; reset selectedLabel when it is no longer in the list or when closetId changes (the component is not remounted on closet switch - only fetchOutfits re-runs via deps at :46).
- src/components/CreateOutfitForm.tsx:13,15 (imports), :78 label state, :168-169 canSubmit requires !!label, :176-182 validation + alert text naming "a label", :186-193 createOutfit({... label ...}), :258-267 `<NativeSelect label="Label" options={OUTFIT_LABELS} ... required />` with no formatLabel. Needs: options from the active closet's list, string typing, loading/empty handling, reset of a selected label that disappears.
- src/services/supabaseOutfitsService.ts:43 `labels: [input.label]` - only needs the type change (and `input.label ? [input.label] : []` if label becomes optional).
- src/services/previewService.ts:270 `labels: [input.label]` (same), :116 passes bundled MyOutfits_Data labels through.
- src/services/supabaseRowMappers.ts:69 `labels: row.labels` - straight passthrough, no narrowing (contrast toClothingItemType at :32 which throws on drift). No change.
- src/constants/MyOutfitsData.tsx:5,17,27,37,47,57 - preview outfits carry lowercase labels ('casual','streetwear','preppy','summer','warm','statement','dressy','elegant','girlie','feminine').
- src/types/supabase.types.ts:372,383,394 outfits.labels string[]; closets block :129-150 has no label column.
- supabase/seed.sql:111,117,132,138,153,159,174,180,195,201 - seeded outfits use only strings that are in OUTFIT_LABELS; closets are inserted with an explicit column list (id, owner_id, closet_name) at :75-84.
- supabase/migrations/20260717025406_create_activity_tablejlzv.sql:141-143 - activity trigger fires AFTER UPDATE OF name, description, labels on outfits.
- Generic components fed by the list: src/components/FilterPills.tsx (generic T extends string, `key={option}` at :39, pill text has textTransform 'capitalize' at :118, aria-label is the raw label at :73); src/components/NativeSelect.tsx / NativeSelect.web.tsx / NativeSelect.shared.ts (generic; defaultFormatLabel at shared :20-25 splits on '_' and upper-cases each word's first letter; native option text also has textTransform 'capitalize' at NativeSelect.tsx:164).
- NOT readers (verified): src/components/outfitDetailPage.tsx (OutfitDetailItem :32-41 has no labels field), src/app/outfit/[id].tsx:76-85 (does not pass labels), src/components/EditOutfitForm.tsx (name/description only), UpdateOutfitInput (dataService.types.ts:323-326), updateOutfit (supabaseOutfitsService.ts:77-80).

(2) CLOSETCONTEXT: HOW CLOSETS LOAD, AND WHERE A LABEL LIST COULD LIVE
- Shapes (dataService.types.ts:269-278): StylistCloset = { closet_id, closet_name }; OwnCloset = StylistCloset + { pass_phrase }.
- ClosetProvider is mounted in src/app/_layout.tsx:62, inside DataModeProvider (:57) and above AppShell/Stack; the comment at :58-61 explains it must not live inside (tabs) or it remounts and drops the stylist selection.
- State (src/context/ClosetContext.tsx): closetMode default 'my-closet' (:38), myCloset: OwnCloset | null (:40), myClosetChecked (:44), stylistClosets: StylistCloset[] | null (:47), selectedStylistClosetId (:49).
- Own closet effect (:51-75): runs only when closetMode === 'my-closet' and a session exists; sets myCloset to null, then dataService.getOwnCloset(userId). Deps [closetMode, dataService, userId, waitingForSession] - so it refetches on every toggle back to My Closet, on user change and on data-mode change, never on focus.
- Stylist effect (:77-97): runs only when closetMode === 'stylist'; nulls stylistClosets and selectedStylistClosetId, then dataService.getStylistClosets(userId). Same deps.
- activeCloset (:100-103) = myCloset in my-closet mode, else the selected stylist closet or the first one.
- Exposed value (:134-163): activeClosetId, activeClosetName, stylistClosets, ownClosetPassphrase (:146), createOwnCloset, regeneratePassphrase, joinCloset... There is no ownClosetId - in stylist mode the context gives consumers no handle on the user's own closet.
- Existing "call service then patch local state" precedents: regeneratePassphrase (:116-120, `setMyCloset({ ...myCloset, pass_phrase })`), createOwnCloset (:107-114), joinCloset (:122-132, appends the returned StylistCloset).
- Live queries that build these shapes: src/services/supabaseClosetsService.ts:16-20 (closet_collaborators -> `closets(id, closet_name)`, row type :5-7, map :27), :32-38 (getOwnCloset), :49-55 (createOwnCloset), :87-89 (joinClosetByPassphrase follow-up select). Preview: previewService.ts:28-32 PREVIEW_CLOSET, :374-399.
- Consumers that would need the list: OutfitsGrid receives closetId as a prop from src/app/(tabs)/outfits/index.tsx:65 and does not call useCloset; CreateOutfitForm already calls useCloset (:72).
- Tabs stay mounted on both platforms (web: src/app/(tabs)/_layout.web.tsx:39-55 hides with display:none), and /outfits/new is a pushed screen in the outfits stack that also stays mounted while the user is on the Settings tab. So an edit made in Settings only reaches OutfitsGrid/CreateOutfitForm through shared state (context) or a refetch on focus.
- Recommendation: carry the list on the closet shape (e.g. outfit_labels: string[] on StylistCloset, inherited by OwnCloset), expose activeClosetLabels from the context (derived from activeCloset), and add an own-closet mutator modelled on regeneratePassphrase that calls the service and then setMyCloset({...}). Labels then arrive atomically with the closet (no separate loading state; OutfitsGrid is only rendered when activeClosetId is set, outfits/index.tsx:54-67) and both consumers re-render immediately because the context value memo depends on myCloset/activeCloset (:151-162). For stylists, the owner's list would otherwise only refresh when closetMode flips to 'stylist' (:77-97); add a refresh on Outfits-tab focus if fresher data matters.

(3) DATASERVICE SHAPE AND CONVENTIONS
- Interface IDataService: dataService.types.ts:342-416. Verb-first camelCase methods (get*/create*/update*/delete*/add*/log*/regenerate*/join*), all return Promise, each with a one-line JSDoc in the interface (multi-line for the optimistic-concurrency ones). Input types are New<X>Input / Update<X>Input with camelCase fields and a "Form data for the ... flow." JSDoc; app-facing entities use snake_case fields (outfit_id, closet_name).
- Live implementation: one module per feature (src/services/supabase<Feature>Service.ts) exporting standalone async functions with the exact interface names; src/services/supabaseService.ts:44-73 only composes them into an object typed IDataService. src/services/dataService.ts:9-16 maps 'live' | 'preview' to the two services; UI gets `dataService` from useDataMode() (src/context/DataModeContext.tsx:12-22; guest => preview).
- Errors: `const { data, error } = await supabase...; if (error) throw error;` - the raw PostgrestError is thrown, not wrapped; each function's JSDoc ends "Throws the Supabase error on failure." Domain failures are `throw new Error('human message')` (supabaseOutfitsService.ts:62). Updates blocked by RLS match zero rows without an error, so writes that must be confirmed select the row back and throw when it is missing: src/services/occConcurrency.ts:22-30 (ConflictError) and supabaseVoiceNotesService.ts:115-117.
- Surfacing: getErrorMessage(err, fallback) at dataService.types.ts:456-467 (needed because PostgrestError is not instanceof Error). Loads set inline error state (`setError(getErrorMessage(err, 'Failed to load outfits.'))`, OutfitsGrid.tsx:43); mutations call showAlert("Couldn't <verb> <thing>", getErrorMessage(err, 'Something went wrong. Please try again.')) (outfitDetailPage.tsx:124); success uses showToast('Outfit updated') (EditOutfitForm.tsx:74) or a showAlert with an OK button (CreateOutfitForm.tsx:211-222). Effects use the `let cancelled = false; ... return () => { cancelled = true; }` guard.
- Preview mirror: class PreviewDataService implements IDataService (previewService.ts:133), exported singleton at :408. Every method is async and returns delay(value) (400 ms, :26, :34-36). Session state lives in module-level arrays/Maps/Sets, each introduced by a `//` comment about its session-only lifetime (:38-80). Unused parameters are prefixed with `_` plus a comment "accepted for interface parity with supabaseService but ignored" (:134-135, :171-173). Because both implementations are typed against IDataService, adding a method to the interface fails compilation until both implement it.
- The Supabase client is created without a Database generic (src/utils/supabase.ts:9-23), so query results are untyped; services type rows by hand with Tables<'...'> from src/types/supabase.types.ts and `.returns<...>()`.

(4) A STORED LABEL THAT IS NOT IN OUTFIT_LABELS
Nothing crashes. mapOutfitRow passes the array through (supabaseRowMappers.ts:69), Outfit.labels is string[], and the only consumer is `outfit.labels.includes(selectedLabel)` (OutfitsGrid.tsx:72). Such an outfit shows under "All" and under no pill. This is already the case in guest mode: every bundled preview outfit has lowercase labels that match none of the Title Case OUTFIT_LABELS, so every pill except "All" shows "No outfits match this filter." (OutfitsGrid.tsx:107) until the guest creates an outfit. The seed data only uses listed labels, so local live data always matches.

(5) CREATE FORM WITH AN EMPTY LABEL LIST
Today: canSubmit requires !!label (CreateOutfitForm.tsx:168-169), so the Save button stays disabled (disabled + aria-disabled at :331,:340) with no explanation; the "Missing information" alert at :176-182 is unreachable because the Pressable is disabled. The picker itself degrades silently: iOS shows an action sheet containing only "Cancel" (NativeSelect.tsx:31-34), web shows a select holding only the disabled placeholder option (NativeSelect.web.tsx:73-75), Android an empty modal list. The form becomes impossible to submit.
Recommendation: when the active closet has no labels, do not render the select; render explanatory text instead (own closet: point to Settings > Edit tags; stylist: say the closet owner has not set up tags) and allow saving with labels: [] - the column accepts an empty array (baseline :182) and the grid handles it. Keep label required when the list is non-empty. On the grid, hide the pills row or show only "All" when the list is empty (precedent: ClosetList.tsx:21-39 only renders pills when there is something to filter). The alternative - forbidding removal of the last tag - is simpler but contradicts "add remove as they want".

(6) STYLISTS CREATING OUTFITS
Yes. RLS "Members can manage outfits" allows any closet member, including collaborators, to insert/update/delete (baseline :379; is_closet_member at :68-79 covers closet_collaborators; outfit_items likewise at :363-367). The UI offers "Create new outfit" in every closet mode on every platform (src/app/(tabs)/outfits/index.tsx:27-39, :72 - unlike the add-item button, which closet/index.tsx:133 hides on web in stylist mode), and CreateOutfitForm writes to activeClosetId (:72, :187), which in stylist mode is the owner's closet. The seed data includes stylist-created outfits (seed.sql:117, 138, 159, 180, 201). So stylists must see the owner's label list for the active closet. Reading is already possible if the list lives on the closets row: "Members can view their closets" (baseline :387) covers collaborators, while "Owners can update their closets" (:403) restricts writes to the owner.

(7) REFRESH / CACHING
- src/state/outfitsRefresh.ts:6-16 is one module-level boolean; markOutfitsDirty is called from CreateOutfitForm.tsx:195, EditOutfitForm.tsx:73, outfitDetailPage.tsx:136, EditClothingItemForm.tsx:137, ClothingItemDetail.tsx:74; the single consumer is OutfitsGrid.tsx:61-69 on focus. Editing the label list does not change any outfit row, so it does not need markOutfitsDirty - unless removing a tag is implemented as also stripping it from outfits, in which case it does.
- consumeOutfitsDirty clears the flag on first read, so the pattern cannot be copied for a value with two consumers (grid and create form); use context state instead.
- Local state a label change must invalidate: OutfitsGrid.selectedLabel (:29) - if the selected label is removed, no pill renders as selected (not even "All", FilterPills.tsx:34) while the grid stays filtered; and CreateOutfitForm.label (:78) - on web the controlled select would hold a value with no matching option (NativeSelect.web.tsx:62) and the stale label would still be submitted.
- ClosetContext's useMemo dependency array (:151-162) must include any new state, or consumers read stale values.
- No other cache holds labels: closet/index.tsx:36-62 and about.tsx:34-55 refetch their own data on focus and do not involve labels.

conventions: DataService methods: verb-first camelCase, async, declared in IDataService (src/services/dataService.types.ts:342-416) with a one-line /** JSDoc */ each; implemented as a standalone exported function in a feature module (supabaseClosetsService.ts etc.), wired into the object literal in supabaseService.ts:44-73, and mirrored as an async method on PreviewDataService.

Live service functions destructure { data, error } and `if (error) throw error;` (raw PostgrestError, never wrapped); their JSDoc ends with 'Throws the Supabase error on failure.' Domain failures use `throw new Error('plain sentence')`.
Writes that RLS may silently reject select the row back (`.select('id').maybeSingle()`) and throw when no row returns - see occConcurrency.ts:22-30 and supabaseVoiceNotesService.ts:115-117.

UI turns any thrown value into text with getErrorMessage(err, fallback) (dataService.types.ts:456-467). Loads: inline error state with 'Failed to load X.'. Mutations: showAlert("Couldn't <verb> <thing>", getErrorMessage(err, 'Something went wrong. Please try again.')). Success: showToast('<Thing> <past participle>') from useToast.

Preview service methods return delay(value); session state is a module-level array/Map/Set introduced by a `//` comment about its session-only lifetime; ignored parameters are prefixed with `_` with a comment 'accepted for interface parity with supabaseService but ignored'.
App-facing entity types use snake_case fields (closet_id, closet_name, outfit_id); form input types are New<X>Input / Update<X>Input with camelCase fields and a 'Form data for the ... flow.' JSDoc.
Constant lists are exported `readonly` arrays / `as const` in dataService.types.ts with a JSDoc saying what drives them (CLOTHING_ITEM_TYPES :22, OUTFIT_LABELS :215).

Context pattern: provider + use<Name>() hook that throws 'use<Name> must be used within a <Name>Provider'; value built with useMemo and an explicit dependency array; mutators call the service then patch local state (ClosetContext.tsx:107-132).
Effects that fetch use `let cancelled = false` with a cleanup setting it true; focus-driven refetches use useFocusEffect(useCallback(...)) from expo-router.
Comments are JSDoc or `//` blocks that explain why, written in full sentences with ' - ' as the dash; no TODO markers.
Theming: layout in StyleSheet.create, colours merged at render from useTheme() (settings.tsx:13-18).

Accessibility props use the aria-* / role form (role="button", aria-label, aria-disabled, aria-selected, role="heading" with aria-level, role="alert" for inline errors, aria-label on ActivityIndicator); text inputs use aria-label `${label}, required`; selected state must be aria-selected on a role="tab" (FilterPills.tsx:55-66).
Tab root screens set aria-hidden={!useIsFocused()} on their root view (settings.tsx:23,40; outfits/index.tsx:12,73).

Migrations: supabase/migrations/<14-digit timestamp>_<snake_name>.sql, opening with a `--` comment block explaining the reason, double-quoted identifiers, `TO "authenticated"` policies named as sentences, helper checks through public.is_closet_member / is_closet_owner, explicit GRANT ALL to anon/authenticated/service_role for new tables and functions; SECURITY DEFINER functions set search_path to 'public'. Latest existing timestamp is 20261013000000.
Length limits are enforced twice: maxLength on the TextInput and a char_length CHECK in the database (20260722031611_add_text_length_constraints.sql).
src/types/supabase.types.ts is updated by hand in the same commit as a migration (commit e1fee32 added the voice_notes block).
gotchas: Tabs and pushed stack screens stay mounted (web hides them with display:none, src/app/(tabs)/_layout.web.tsx:39-55), so OutfitsGrid and an open /outfits/new form live through a Settings edit. Their local state goes stale: OutfitsGrid.selectedLabel (OutfitsGrid.tsx:29) and CreateOutfitForm.label (CreateOutfitForm.tsx:78) must be reset when the value leaves the list.
If the selected pill's label is removed, FilterPills shows no pill as selected (not even All, FilterPills.tsx:34) while the grid stays filtered and may show 'No outfits match this filter.'
OutfitsGrid is not remounted when closetId changes, so selectedLabel carries over between closets; harmless with one global list, wrong with per-closet lists.
On web a controlled select whose value matches no option (NativeSelect.web.tsx:62) displays the placeholder while React state still holds the removed label, which would then be submitted.

defaultFormatLabel (NativeSelect.shared.ts:20-25) turns 'beach_day' into 'Beach Day' and upper-cases the first letter; native option text and pill text also apply textTransform 'capitalize' (NativeSelect.tsx:164, FilterPills.tsx:118). User-typed tags will not display verbatim unless CreateOutfitForm passes formatLabel={v => v} and the pill style is addressed. Pill aria-label is the raw string, so the spoken and visible forms can differ.

FilterPills uses key={option} (FilterPills.tsx:39) and NativeSelect uses the option as key/value, so duplicate labels break rendering; the list must be unique. Filtering is an exact case-sensitive match (OutfitsGrid.tsx:72), so 'casual' and 'Casual' are different tags and whitespace matters - trim and de-duplicate (ideally case-insensitively) on input.

Stripping a removed tag from outfits rows would fire the activity trigger for every touched outfit (create_activity migration :141-143, 'X edited outfit Y' entries in Logs) and bump updated_at via set_outfits_updated_at, causing ConflictError for anyone with those outfits open. Leaving old strings on outfits is harmless (they appear under All).

Do not log tag edits into activity_logs with a new item_type: the table has a check constraint (create_activity migration :16) and toActivityItemType throws on unknown values (dataService.types.ts:248-251), which makes getActivityLog fail for the whole feed (supabaseActivityService.ts:14-16) - including on already-installed app builds.
ClosetContext does not expose the user's own closet id; in stylist mode activeClosetId is the owner's closet. A Settings > Edit tags screen for 'my tags' needs the own closet explicitly.

myCloset is only refetched while closetMode === 'my-closet' (ClosetContext.tsx:51-75). If a user signs out and another signs in while closetMode is 'stylist', myCloset still holds the previous user's closet until they toggle back. Anything reading the own closet from context in stylist mode must account for this (fetch fresh via dataService.getOwnCloset(userId), as outfitDetailPage.tsx:81 does, or load the own closet independent of mode).
Switching to My Closet sets myCloset to null before refetching (ClosetContext.tsx:55), so a label list carried on it is briefly unavailable; consumers must tolerate null.

Stylist closets are only refetched when closetMode flips to 'stylist' (ClosetContext.tsx:77-97); an owner's tag edit will not reach a stylist's running session without an extra refresh. joinCloset appends the object returned by joinClosetByPassphrase (:122-132), so that return value must also include the label list.

A non-owner UPDATE on closets returns zero rows and no error under 'Owners can update their closets' (baseline :403). Without selecting the row back the UI would report success while nothing was saved.
A user with no closet of their own (needsOwnClosetSetup, ClosetContext.tsx:105) - for example a pure stylist - has nothing to attach tags to; the edit screen needs an empty state.
closets has no unique constraint on owner_id (baseline :226-232); one-closet-per-user is assumed by getOwnCloset's maybeSingle (supabaseClosetsService.ts:36), which errors if two exist.
consumeOutfitsDirty clears the flag on first read (outfitsRefresh.ts:12-16); copying that pattern for labels would starve whichever of the two consumers reads second.
ClosetContext's useMemo dependency array (:151-162) is maintained by hand; new state or mutators that are not listed give consumers stale values.

Guest mode: bundled preview outfits have lowercase labels that match none of the default tags (MyOutfitsData.tsx:17-57), so every pill but All is empty there today. previewService has no label-list state yet and getStylistClosets returns [] (:374-376).

Already-installed iOS builds keep the hardcoded list and will continue writing those ten strings to outfits.labels in any closet, regardless of the owner's custom list. Outfits can therefore carry tags the owner removed; the app must keep tolerating unknown strings.
The Supabase client has no Database generic (src/utils/supabase.ts:9), so a misspelled column or table name compiles and only fails at runtime.

supabase/schema.sql is a partially maintained snapshot (updated in commit 591ae6a, not in the voice-notes commit; it lacks activity_logs, updated_at and voice_notes) and supabase/schema_remote_dump.sql is empty - neither is authoritative; migrations are.

supabaseClosetsService.ts:64 calls an RPC named regenerate_closet_passphrase that is defined in no migration and absent from supabase.types.ts; it is not a reliable template for a new RPC (the UI never calls regeneratePassphrase).

showAlert on web maps to window.alert / window.confirm, with OK bound to the first non-cancel button (src/utils/alert.ts:18-34); a remove-tag confirmation must be built with a cancel-styled button plus one action button.
The Home screen's forms use `err instanceof Error ? err.message : ...` (src/app/(tabs)/index.tsx:158, 223), which drops Supabase error messages; use getErrorMessage instead of copying that.
tsconfig moduleSuffixes lists .web before the bare suffix (tsconfig.json), so TypeScript checks NativeSelect callers against NativeSelect.web.tsx; both builds share NativeSelectProps to stay aligned.

With an empty option list the iOS picker opens an action sheet containing only Cancel (NativeSelect.tsx:31-34) and the Save button is permanently disabled with no spoken reason (CreateOutfitForm.tsx:168-169, 331-340).

codeMaps.area: Navigation + Logs screen (expo-router tabs, nested stacks, web nav/shell, deep-link config) - what it takes to remove the "Logs" tab and reach it from a button in Settings
codeMaps.summary:
READ-ONLY mapping; nothing was built or run, so runtime claims are from reading app code plus installed library source (expo-router 55.0.17, @react-navigation/bottom-tabs 7.18.16, native-stack 7.18.8, elements 2.9.38).

WHAT EXISTS
- Root: src/app/_layout.tsx:66-78 is a root Stack: "(tabs)" (headerShown false), item/[id], item/edit/[id], outfit/[id], outfit/edit/[id] inside Stack.Protected guard={signedIn}; sign-in; +not-found. AppShell wraps it (pass-through on native, site chrome on web).
- Tabs: two platform files declare the same five screens in the same order (index, closet, outfits, about, settings): src/app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx:22-68 (native, icons, bottom bar) and src/app/(tabs)/_layout.web.tsx:30-34 (web, tabBar={() => null}). The Tabs-level header is HeaderBanner (native _layout.tsx:19; web _layout.web.tsx:26-27). closet and outfits set headerShown:false because they are directories with their own Stack; index, about, settings are single files using HeaderBanner.
- Logs screen: src/app/(tabs)/about.tsx (component AboutScreen, :20). Self-contained: reads activeClosetId from useCloset, refetches dataService.getActivityLog(activeClosetId) in useFocusEffect on every focus (:34-55, clears entries to null first so a spinner shows each time), renders loading/error/empty/list states (:57-107), root View has aria-hidden={!isFocused} (:110). It sets no title itself; "Logs" comes only from the Tabs.Screen options. No other file links to it except the tab bar and the web nav.
- Settings: src/app/(tabs)/settings.tsx, one ScrollView with cards Account (:42-58), Appearance (:60-99), Sign out button (:101-107); card titles are role="heading" aria-level={2}; root has aria-hidden={!isFocused} (:40).
- Web nav: src/components/HeaderNav.web.tsx NAV_ITEMS (:11-17) renders expo-router Link elements; isActive (:19-22) is prefix based, so /settings/logs would mark "Settings" as aria-current="page".

(1) NESTED STACK PATTERN (closet/, outfits/)
- closet/_layout.tsx and outfits/_layout.tsx are identical (:5-23): export const unstable_settings = { initialRouteName: 'index' }; a bare Stack with screenOptions { headerTitleAlign: 'center', headerStyle.backgroundColor: stylist ? theme.stylist : theme.surface, headerTintColor: stylist ? theme.onStylist : theme.textPrimary } from useCloset() + useTheme(). No Stack.Screen children are declared; routes are auto-discovered.
- Titles come from each screen rendering Stack.Screen options: closet/index.tsx:131-136 (title + headerRight), closet/new.tsx:7 (title only), outfits/index.tsx:72, outfits/new.tsx:7.
- Back buttons: sub-screens set NO headerLeft. Native gets the UINavigationBar back button; web gets react-navigation's HeaderBackButton (native-stack NativeStackView.tsx:127-151) whose label is "<previous title>, back" (elements HeaderBackButton.tsx:35) and which renders as role="link" because an href is passed (PlatformPressable.tsx:168). The app's own src/components/HeaderBackButton.tsx is used only by root-stack detail routes (item/edit/[id].tsx:10, outfit/[id].tsx:97, outfit/edit/[id].tsx:10, ClothingItemDetail.tsx:364) because those can be opened cold; its fallback is router.replace('/') i.e. Home (:13-17).
- Web title element: elements HeaderTitle.tsx:21-24 renders role="heading" aria-level="1".
- To match exactly, settings needs: src/app/(tabs)/settings/_layout.tsx as a copy of closet/_layout.tsx; settings/index.tsx (current settings.tsx body plus Stack.Screen options title 'Settings', keep aria-hidden={!isFocused}); settings/logs.tsx (about.tsx body plus Stack.Screen title); settings/tags.tsx; and headerShown:false added to the "settings" Tabs.Screen in BOTH (tabs)/_layout.tsx:60-68 and (tabs)/_layout.web.tsx:34, otherwise HeaderBanner and the stack header both render. The _layout.tsx is mandatory: without it settings/index, settings/logs, settings/tags each become their own tab. Route name stays "settings" and URL /settings is unchanged.
- Visible side effect: Settings changes from HeaderBanner (web: left-aligned 24px h1, HeaderBanner.web.tsx:30-36,53-56) to the react-navigation header (centred title), the same as My Closet/Outfits today.

(2) HIDDEN TAB (href: null) VS REMOVED ROUTE
- href:null (expo-router TabsClient.js:19-40) only sets tabBarItemStyle display:none and a tabBarButton returning null. The route still exists, /about still resolves, is still exported, and is still a tab. It is irrelevant on web, where the whole bar is already null.
- Two concrete problems with a hidden tab: (a) iOS VoiceOver labels are "<label>, tab, N of routes.length" (BottomTabBar.tsx:429-435), and routes includes hidden tabs, so VoiceOver would say "Settings, tab, 5 of 5" with four visible tabs. (b) Reaching it is a tab jump, not a push: no back button, and neither layout sets backBehavior so the default 'firstRoute' applies (routers SwitchRouter.tsx:183,98-104) and router.back() goes to Home, not Settings.
- Removing only the Tabs.Screen line but keeping about.tsx does NOT remove the tab: undeclared files are appended automatically (useScreens.js:114-115), giving a tab labelled "about" with a placeholder icon.
- Keeping the Tabs.Screen line but deleting the file logs a dev warning "[Layout children]: No route named "about" exists" (useScreens.js:73-76).
- Deleting/moving the file and both Tabs.Screen lines makes /about unmatched: native shows +not-found (root _layout.tsx:77); on web Cloudflare serves 404.html, which scripts/post-export.js:12-17 copies from +not-found.html.

(3) EVERY /about, "about", "Logs" REFERENCE - see everyReferenceThatMustChange. Checked and clean: public/sw.js (no route list; only SHELL_URL '/' at :18,31 is precached, navigations are network-first), public/manifest.json (shortcuts are /closet and /outfits only, :33-44), public/_headers, public/.well-known/assetlinks.json (no paths), scripts/post-export.js (:25-31 checks files, not routes), src/app/+html.tsx, src/app/+not-found.tsx, src/app/_layout.tsx, README.md, example/. /settings is in neither the AASA file nor the Android intent filters today.

(4) WEB HIDING / FOCUS HANDLING
- The web tab view keeps visited tabs mounted (BottomTabView.tsx:343-352: absoluteFill, zIndex -1, pointerEvents none).
- _layout.web.tsx:21 passes screenLayout wrapping every tab scene in TabScene (:47-55), which applies display:none + aria-hidden when useIsFocused() is false. screenLayout wraps the route component (core useDescriptors.tsx:241-270), so for a directory tab it covers the nested Stack and its headers.
- The Tabs-level header is outside screenLayout, so it is gated separately with navigation.isFocused() (_layout.web.tsx:26-27).
- Inside a stack on web, non-focused screens get display:none (native-stack NativeStackView.tsx:158-168) and elements Screen adds aria-hidden={!focused} (Screen.tsx:71). So settings/index is removed from the accessibility tree and tab order while logs/tags is on top.
- Each tab root screen also sets aria-hidden={!isFocused} on its own root (index.tsx:39, about.tsx:110, settings.tsx:40, closet/index.tsx:138, outfits/index.tsx:73); isFocused checks the parent chain (core useNavigationCache.tsx:219-228). Pushed sub-screens (closet/new, outfits/new) do not do this.
- A new sub-screen under (tabs)/settings/ therefore needs: to live inside that directory, to use the nested Stack header with a title set via Stack.Screen, and to not leave a Modal open when it loses focus (react-native-web Modal portals outside the scene).

(5) TITLE / HEADING ANNOUNCEMENT ON WEB
- document.title is never set: expo-router disables it (ExpoRoot.js:64-66), +html.tsx has no title element (comment :42-44), and src has no document.title or Head usage.
- Route changes are announced by useAnnounceRouteChange in AppShell.web.tsx:71-98: on every usePathname() change except the first render it focuses the first h1/h2/[role="heading"] inside #main-content whose offsetParent is not null (falls back to main), after setting tabIndex=-1.
- For a nested-stack screen the first visible heading is the stack header title, so /settings/logs would focus and announce "Logs" provided the header is shown and has a title.
- On iOS native, stack push/pop posts the screen-changed notification automatically.

(6) TYPED ROUTES
- experiments.typedRoutes is on (app.config.ts:148-151) and tsconfig includes .expo/types and expo-env.d.ts (tsconfig.json:14-19), but both are gitignored and absent here (.expo contains only web/cache).
- They are generated only by `expo start`, not by `expo export`. Without them Href is `string | HrefObject` (expo-router typed-routes/types.d.ts:8-9,51-53), so `npx tsc --noEmit` in this environment will not catch a stale '/about' or a mistyped '/settings/logs'.
- On a dev machine with generated types, removing about.tsx drops '/about' from the union and HeaderNav.web.tsx:6 plus :15 become type errors; '/settings/logs' and '/settings/tags' become valid as soon as the files exist.

## (1) Definitions, policies, grants, triggers, functions

**closets** (baseline:114-120)
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "public"."closets" (
    "id" "uuid" DEFAULT "gen_random_uuid"() NOT NULL,
    "owner_id" "uuid" NOT NULL,
    "closet_name" "text" NOT NULL,
    "pass_phrase" "text" DEFAULT "substr"("md5"((("random"())::"text" || ("clock_timestamp"())::"text")), 1, 10) NOT NULL,
    "created_at" timestamp with time zone DEFAULT "now"() NOT NULL
);
```
- Constraints: "closets_pass_phrase_key" UNIQUE (baseline:226-227), "closets_pkey" (231-232), "closets_owner_id_fkey" -> users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE (286-287).
- It has no updated_at, no length check on closet_name, no unique on owner_id, and no trigger of any kind.
- RLS is enabled (baseline:442). Policies:
  - 387: `"Members can view their closets" FOR SELECT TO "authenticated" USING (("public"."is_closet_member"("id") OR ("owner_id" = "auth"."uid"())))`

  - 415: `"Users can create closets they own" FOR INSERT ... WITH CHECK (("owner_id" = "auth"."uid"()))`
- Grants: baseline:664-666.

**closet_collaborators** (baseline:103-108): id, user_id, closet_id, created_at.

**outfits** (baseline:176-185): id, closet_id, created_by_user_id, name, description, `"labels" "text"[] DEFAULT '{}'::"text"[] NOT NULL`, compliment_count, created_at.

**Functions**
- is_closet_member (baseline:68-79) and is_closet_owner (85-93): `LANGUAGE "sql" STABLE SECURITY DEFINER SET "search_path" TO 'public'`, both keyed on auth.uid().

**Grant pattern** — three lines per object, anon included; anon is blocked only because every policy is `TO "authenticated"`:
```sql
GRANT ALL ON TABLE "public"."voice_notes" TO "anon";
GRANT ALL ON TABLE "public"."voice_notes" TO "authenticated";
GRANT ALL ON TABLE "public"."voice_notes" TO "service_role";          -- 20261013000000:55-57
GRANT ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."join_closet_by_passphrase"("target_pass_phrase" "text") TO "anon";  -- + authenticated, service_role (20260721000000:39-41)
```
- Each function also gets `ALTER FUNCTION ... OWNER TO "postgres";` and each table `ALTER TABLE ... OWNER TO "postgres";`.
- There is no REVOKE anywhere and no column-level grant.
- config.toml:19-24 says new entities are NOT auto-exposed to the API roles when auto_expose_new_tables is unset, so explicit grants on a new table or function are mandatory. Baseline:718-741 also has ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES; I could not verify which wins on remote.
- A new column on closets needs no grant, because the table-level GRANT ALL covers it.

## (2) How closets are created, and seeding/backfill

- Closets are created by a plain client insert: `supabase.from('closets').insert({ owner_id: userId, closet_name: closetName }).select('id, closet_name, pass_phrase').single()` (src/services/supabaseClosetsService.ts:48-56). It runs under policy baseline:415. There is no trigger and no RPC.
- Call chain: NewClosetForm (src/app/(tabs)/index.tsx:137) -> ClosetContext.createOwnCloset (src/context/ClosetContext.tsx:107-114).
- seed.sql:75-84 inserts five closets directly, with no JWT, so auth.uid() is NULL there.
- Column design: the column DEFAULT seeds new closets, and on PG17 `ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT <constant array> NOT NULL` backfills existing rows as a metadata-only change.
- Table design: an AFTER INSERT trigger on closets seeds new closets, and a one-off `INSERT ... SELECT closets CROSS JOIN unnest(...)` in the same migration backfills existing ones.
  - The trigger should be SECURITY DEFINER, like log_outfit_activity, which inserts into activity_logs although that table has only a SELECT policy (20260717025406:42).
  - It must not depend on auth.uid(), because of seed.sql.
- seed.sql needs no edit either way; it runs after migrations on `supabase db reset` (config.toml:66-71).

## (3) Migration conventions

- **Naming:** `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_snake_case.sql`. The last two are 20261012000000 and 20261013000000; a new one must sort after the latter, e.g. `20261111000000_closet_outfit_labels.sql`.
- **Header:** a `--` prose block explaining why. Only 20260722031611 lacks one.
- **Quoting:** pg_dump style. Every identifier, type and function is double-quoted and schema-qualified (`"public"."outfits"`, `"uuid"`, `"gen_random_uuid"()`, `"auth"."uid"()`, `"char_length"("name")`), with uppercase keywords. Function bodies are lowercase, unquoted, with `public.` qualification, `v_` locals, `target_` args and `raise exception '...'`.
- **Idempotency:** not general.
  - Functions always use `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION`.
  - Tables: `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` in activity_logs (20260717025406:6), plain `CREATE TABLE` in voice_notes (20261013000000:11).
  - Plain `CREATE POLICY`, `CREATE TRIGGER`, `CREATE INDEX`, `ADD COLUMN`, `ADD CONSTRAINT`.
  - `CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER` and `DROP POLICY IF EXISTS` appear only where remote had hand-made drift (20260721010000:8, 20260721203955:10-21).
  - The data insert uses `ON CONFLICT ("id") DO NOTHING` (20261013000000:62-64).
- **Constraint names:** `<table>_pkey`, `<table>_<col>_fkey`, `<table>_<cols>_key` (unique), `<table>_<col>_check`, `<table>_<col>_length`, or descriptive ("voice_notes_one_target", "voice_notes_duration_range"). Indexes are `<table>_<cols>_idx`. Triggers are "set_<table>_updated_at" and "log_<x>_activity_trigger".
- **Functions:** `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."f"("target_x" "uuid") RETURNS "text"` / `LANGUAGE "plpgsql" SECURITY DEFINER` / `SET "search_path" TO 'public'` / `AS $$ ... $$;` then OWNER TO, then three GRANTs. SECURITY DEFINER is used only when justified in the header; the invoker RPC says so explicitly (20260722025112:4-6).
- **Length constraints:** `ADD CONSTRAINT "outfits_name_length" CHECK ("char_length"("name") <= 100)`, several per ALTER TABLE (20260722031611).
- **updated_at:** `ADD COLUMN "updated_at" timestamp with time zone DEFAULT "now"() NOT NULL` plus a `BEFORE UPDATE ... FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION "public"."set_updated_at"()` trigger (20260722040000:21-33).
- **New table template** (voice_notes, 20261013000000:11-57): inline named constraints, OWNER TO, indexes, ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, one commented policy per operation, three grants.

## (4) activity_logs

- Only two logging triggers exist (20260717025406:141-148): on outfits `AFTER INSERT OR DELETE OR UPDATE OF "name", "description", "labels"`, and on clothing_items.
- There is no trigger on closets or closet_collaborators. A new closets column or a new labels table logs nothing and breaks nothing.
- activity_logs.item_type is CHECKed to 'outfit' | 'clothing_item' (line 16), and the client throws on anything else (src/services/dataService.types.ts:248-251). Do not log label edits there without widening both.
- Any statement with `labels` in an outfits UPDATE SET list has two side effects per row, even if the value is unchanged:
  - it inserts an 'edited' activity row;
  - set_outfits_updated_at bumps updated_at, which invalidates other clients' optimistic-concurrency tokens (src/services/occConcurrency.ts:22-30).
- So stripping a removed label from outfits, or normalising labels in a migration, would spam the Logs screen. In a migration auth.uid() is NULL, so those rows would have a null actor.
- The trigger function uses `v_row public.outfits`. The outfits table is not being altered, so that is unaffected.

## (6) Storage options

**(a) text[] column on closets**
```sql
ALTER TABLE "public"."closets"
    ADD COLUMN "outfit_labels" "text"[] DEFAULT ARRAY['Girly/Romantic'::"text", 'Work'::"text", 'Casual'::"text", 'Date Night'::"text", 'Athleisure'::"text", 'Formal Event'::"text", 'Street Style'::"text", 'Minimalist Chic'::"text", 'Artsy'::"text", 'Boho'::"text"] NOT NULL,
    ADD CONSTRAINT "closets_outfit_labels_count" CHECK (("cardinality"("outfit_labels") <= 50));
-- plus two RPCs, e.g.:
-- add_closet_outfit_label(target_closet_id uuid, target_label text) returns text[]  SECURITY DEFINER, search_path public
--   if not public.is_closet_member(target_closet_id) then raise exception 'Not authorized'; end if;
--   v_label := btrim(target_label); reject empty or char_length > 40;
--   update public.closets set outfit_labels = array_append(outfit_labels, v_label)
--    where id = target_closet_id
--      and not exists (select 1 from unnest(outfit_labels) l where lower(l) = lower(v_label))
--    returning outfit_labels into v_labels;  -- null => 'That tag already exists'
-- remove_closet_outfit_label(...): set outfit_labels = array_remove(outfit_labels, target_label) ... returning
```
Client: `supabase.rpc('add_closet_outfit_label', { target_closet_id, target_label })`. Read with `.from('closets').select('outfit_labels').eq('id', closetId).single()`, which members may do under policy 387.

**(b) closet_outfit_labels table**
```sql
CREATE TABLE "public"."closet_outfit_labels" (
    "id" "uuid" DEFAULT "gen_random_uuid"() NOT NULL,
    "closet_id" "uuid" NOT NULL,
    "name" "text" NOT NULL,
    "sort_order" integer DEFAULT 1000 NOT NULL,
    "created_at" timestamp with time zone DEFAULT "now"() NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT "closet_outfit_labels_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("id"),
    CONSTRAINT "closet_outfit_labels_closet_id_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("closet_id") REFERENCES "public"."closets"("id") ON DELETE CASCADE,
    CONSTRAINT "closet_outfit_labels_name_length" CHECK (("char_length"("name") >= 1 AND "char_length"("name") <= 40)),
    CONSTRAINT "closet_outfit_labels_name_trimmed" CHECK (("name" = "btrim"("name")))
);
ALTER TABLE "public"."closet_outfit_labels" OWNER TO "postgres";
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "closet_outfit_labels_closet_id_lower_name_key" ON "public"."closet_outfit_labels" ("closet_id", "lower"("name"));
ALTER TABLE "public"."closet_outfit_labels" ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY "Members can view closet outfit labels" ON "public"."closet_outfit_labels" FOR SELECT TO "authenticated" USING ("public"."is_closet_member"("closet_id"));
CREATE POLICY "Members can add closet outfit labels" ON "public"."closet_outfit_labels" FOR INSERT TO "authenticated" WITH CHECK ("public"."is_closet_member"("closet_id"));
CREATE POLICY "Members can remove closet outfit labels" ON "public"."closet_outfit_labels" FOR DELETE TO "authenticated" USING ("public"."is_closet_member"("closet_id"));
GRANT ALL ON TABLE "public"."closet_outfit_labels" TO "anon";  -- + "authenticated", "service_role"
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."seed_closet_outfit_labels"() RETURNS "trigger"
    LANGUAGE "plpgsql" SECURITY DEFINER
    SET "search_path" TO 'public'
    AS $$
begin
  insert into public.closet_outfit_labels (closet_id, name, sort_order)
  select new.id, l.name, l.ord
  from unnest(array['Girly/Romantic','Work','Casual','Date Night','Athleisure','Formal Event','Street Style','Minimalist Chic','Artsy','Boho']) with ordinality as l(name, ord)
  on conflict do nothing;
  return new;
end;
$$;
-- OWNER TO postgres + 3 GRANT ALL ON FUNCTION
CREATE TRIGGER "seed_closet_outfit_labels_trigger" AFTER INSERT ON "public"."closets" FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION "public"."seed_closet_outfit_labels"();
INSERT INTO "public"."closet_outfit_labels" ("closet_id", "name", "sort_order")
SELECT c.id, l.name, l.ord FROM public.closets c CROSS JOIN unnest(ARRAY[...same ten...]) WITH ORDINALITY AS l(name, ord)
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
```
Client, following the voice-notes service (src/services/supabaseVoiceNotesService.ts:52-59, 115-117):
- List: `.from('closet_outfit_labels').select('id, name').eq('closet_id', id).order('sort_order').order('created_at')`
- Add: `.insert({ closet_id, name }).select('id, name').single()`; error.code '23505' means "already exists".
- Remove: `.delete().eq('id', labelId).select('id').maybeSingle()`; null means already gone or not permitted.

**Tradeoffs**

| Concern | (a) column | (b) table |
|---|---|---|
| RLS | Reuses policy 387 for reads. Writes need RPCs, because stylists cannot UPDATE closets (403) | Per-operation policies; owner-only vs members is a one-word switch (is_closet_owner / is_closet_member); no RPC |
| Concurrent edits | A direct array UPDATE is whole-value last-write-wins, and closets has no updated_at (OccTable is only 'outfits' and 'clothing_items', occConcurrency.ts:5). A single-statement RPC serialises on the row lock | Single-row INSERT/DELETE commute; a duplicate add gives 23505 |
| Case-insensitive uniqueness | Only inside the RPC, or via an IMMUTABLE validator in a CHECK | Declarative unique index on lower(name) |
| Length limits | CHECK cannot subquery array elements; needs a helper function or RPC validation | Plain CHECK, same style as 20260722031611 |
| Ordering | Array order is free | Needs sort_order: seeded rows share created_at because now() is transaction time |
| Backfill and new closets | Automatic via DEFAULT | Trigger plus backfill insert |
| Size of change | Smallest migration, but two RPCs | More SQL, but it is the voice_notes pattern |

Both designs leave outfits.labels as free text, so removing a label orphans it on existing outfits.

Recommendation: (b). It matches the most recent precedent and makes every invariant declarative.

## (7) Owner-only UPDATE policy on closets

- Policy 403 is row-level only, and baseline:665 grants ALL on the table with no column grants.
- An owner can therefore PATCH their own row directly through PostgREST and set:
  - pass_phrase to anything, including weak or empty-ish values; only UNIQUE and NOT NULL apply, and a 23505 leaks that another closet uses that phrase;
  - closet_name with no length cap;
  - created_at;
  - id, if no child rows exist.
- owner_id cannot be moved to another user, because WITH CHECK requires the new owner_id = auth.uid().
- Non-owners match no UPDATE policy: zero rows are updated and no error is raised.
- With design (a), an owner could write arbitrary arrays (thousands of entries, duplicates, huge strings) and bypass RPC-only validation. So (a) must both go through RPCs, for atomicity and stylist access, and enforce invariants in a table CHECK or trigger.
- Design (b) does not touch closets, so this does not arise.
- The app never issues a direct UPDATE on closets (supabaseClosetsService.ts:33, 50, 87 are select/insert only).
- Separately, policy 387 lets any member SELECT the owner's pass_phrase. "Only owners can see their own passphrase" (dataService.types.ts:275) is a client convention, not something RLS enforces. This is pre-existing and out of scope.

conventions: Migration filename is supabase/migrations/YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_snake_case_description.sql and must sort after 20261013000000_voice_notes.sql (for example 20261111000000_closet_outfit_labels.sql). Use one migration per feature, as voice_notes did with table, policies, grants and bucket together.

Start the migration with a `--` prose header explaining what and why, including the reason for any SECURITY DEFINER and who is allowed to do what. Put a short `--` comment above each policy, as in 20261013000000:36-53.

DDL uses pg_dump-style quoting: every identifier, type and function call is double-quoted and schema-qualified ("public"."closets", "uuid", "text"[], "gen_random_uuid"(), "now"(), "auth"."uid"(), "char_length"("name")), with uppercase SQL keywords and `timestamp with time zone` unquoted.

Function bodies are lowercase unquoted plpgsql/sql with explicit `public.` qualification, `target_`-prefixed arguments, `v_`-prefixed locals, `raise exception 'Human readable message'`, and auth.uid() for the caller.

Function declaration shape: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."name"("target_x" "uuid") RETURNS "type" / LANGUAGE "plpgsql" SECURITY DEFINER / SET "search_path" TO 'public' / AS $$ ... $$; then ALTER FUNCTION ... OWNER TO "postgres"; then three GRANT ALL ON FUNCTION lines to "anon", "authenticated", "service_role".

Use SECURITY DEFINER only when RLS cannot express the rule, and say why in the header. Otherwise write an invoker function and say so explicitly, as 20260722025112:4-6 does. Any SECURITY DEFINER RPC must check auth.uid(), ownership or membership itself, because EXECUTE is granted to anon too.

A new table gets: CREATE TABLE with inline named constraints, ALTER TABLE ... OWNER TO "postgres", indexes, ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, one CREATE POLICY per operation scoped TO "authenticated" using "public"."is_closet_member"("closet_id") or is_closet_owner, then GRANT ALL ON TABLE to "anon", "authenticated", "service_role" on three lines.
Policy names are sentence-case English: "Members can view ...", "Members can add ...", "Owners can ...", "Users can ...".

Constraint and index names: <table>_pkey, <table>_<col>_fkey (to closets with ON DELETE CASCADE), <table>_<cols>_key for unique, <table>_<col>_check for value lists, <table>_<col>_length for length caps, descriptive names such as voice_notes_one_target, and <table>_<cols>_idx for indexes.

Trigger names: set_<table>_updated_at, log_<thing>_activity_trigger, on_auth_user_created. Trigger functions RETURNS "trigger", and those that write across RLS are SECURITY DEFINER with search_path public.

Migrations are run-once, not idempotent: plain CREATE POLICY, CREATE TRIGGER, ADD COLUMN and ADD CONSTRAINT. Functions always use CREATE OR REPLACE. Data inserts use ON CONFLICT ... DO NOTHING. IF EXISTS / OR REPLACE on triggers and policies is reserved for objects that may already exist on remote from hand edits.
Primary keys are "id" "uuid" DEFAULT "gen_random_uuid"() NOT NULL; timestamps are "created_at" timestamp with time zone DEFAULT "now"() NOT NULL.

activity_logs.item_type is CHECK-limited to 'outfit' | 'clothing_item' (20260717025406:16), and the client throws on any other value (src/services/dataService.types.ts:248-251). Logging label edits there would break the Logs screen unless both are widened.

seed.sql inserts closets with no JWT (seed.sql:75-84), so auth.uid() is NULL. A seeding trigger on closets must not reference auth.uid() or rely on RLS passing; make it SECURITY DEFINER and use NEW.id only.

A table-design seeding trigger inserts all ten rows in one transaction, so they share the same created_at (now() is transaction start). Ordering by created_at alone is nondeterministic for the defaults; add a sort_order column or a secondary sort.

For a unique index on (closet_id, lower(name)), PostgREST upsert/on_conflict cannot target an expression index. Use a plain insert and map error code 23505 to 'tag already exists'. In SQL, use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING without a conflict target for the trigger and backfill.

outfits.labels is free text[] with no FK or check (baseline:182). Removing a closet label leaves it on existing outfits. Since labels are only used for the filter in src/components/OutfitsGrid.tsx:72, those outfits become reachable only via 'All'. Matching is exact and case-sensitive, so removing 'Work' and re-adding 'work' will not match old outfits.

The Create Outfit form requires a label (src/components/CreateOutfitForm.tsx:78, 261). If a closet's label list can be emptied, outfit creation is blocked unless the UI prevents removing the last label or the label becomes optional. Neither design enforces a minimum in the DB.

The 'Owners can update their closets' policy (baseline:403) plus table-wide GRANT ALL (baseline:665) lets an owner PATCH any column of their own closets row except owner_id. With a column-on-closets design, RPC-only validation is bypassable by a direct update, so invariants must live in a CHECK or trigger. Stylists cannot UPDATE closets at all, so member edits would need a SECURITY DEFINER RPC.

A direct array update from the client is a whole-value overwrite, and closets has no updated_at (src/services/occConcurrency.ts:5 covers only outfits and clothing_items). Two devices adding different tags would silently lose one. Use single-statement RPCs for the column design, or row-per-label inserts and deletes for the table design.

Pre-existing drift: src/services/supabaseClosetsService.ts:64 calls RPC 'regenerate_closet_passphrase', which is defined in no migration and absent from src/types/supabase.types.ts:496-507. It existed only in an older hand-written schema.sql (git show 41557b6:supabase/schema.sql lines 204-233) and was dropped from the types in commit 2baf8cd. It is not referenced by any screen (only src/context/ClosetContext.tsx:116-120). Do not copy it as a living pattern, and do not expect it in a migration-built or PGlite DB.
supabase/schema.sql is a stale snapshot, not a source of truth, and supabase/schema_remote_dump.sql is empty. Do not derive the current schema from either; use the migrations.

The supabase client is untyped (src/utils/supabase.ts:9 has no <Database> generic). A typo in a table, column or RPC name compiles fine and fails only at runtime, and the types file will not catch a mismatch with the migration.

Any closet member can already SELECT the whole closets row, including pass_phrase (baseline:387). Adding label reads to closets selects for stylists is fine, but do not widen what the stylist embed returns beyond the needed columns (src/services/supabaseClosetsService.ts:18).

For a PGlite check of the migration, the baseline needs stubs: roles anon/authenticated/service_role/postgres; schemas auth, extensions, storage, vault; auth.uid() reading request.jwt.claims; auth.users; storage.objects and storage.buckets; publication supabase_realtime. Skip the CREATE EXTENSION lines (baseline:20-41) and ALTER PUBLICATION (baseline:468). The baseline sets search_path to '' (line 9), so later statements must stay schema-qualified.

is_closet_member and is_closet_owner are STABLE SECURITY DEFINER and depend on auth.uid() (baseline:68-93). They return false for anon and for service/migration contexts, so backfill SQL must not go through them.

Preview-mode outfits carry labels such as 'casual' and 'streetwear' (src/constants/MyOutfitsData.tsx:17-57) that are not in the ten generic labels, so the pills never match bundled preview outfits. This is pre-existing; a preview-mode label list should start from OUTFIT_LABELS regardless.

openQuestions: Who may edit a closet's tags: the owner only, or any member including stylists? README.md:14 shows the product owner is undecided ('make new tags? who can make? admin only?'). With the table design this is a one-word policy choice (is_closet_owner vs is_closet_member); with the column design, member edits force SECURITY DEFINER RPCs.

Which closet does Settings > Edit tags act on: always the user's own closet, or activeClosetId (which can be a stylist closet, src/context/ClosetContext.tsx:100-103)? A pure stylist with no own closet has nothing to edit in the first case.

When a tag is removed, should it also be stripped from existing outfits? Stripping creates one 'edited' activity row and an updated_at bump per outfit. Leaving it means those outfits are no longer reachable through any filter pill. I recommend leaving them untouched; this needs a product decision.

May a closet end up with zero tags? The create-outfit form currently requires one (src/components/CreateOutfitForm.tsx:78, 261). Either block removing the last tag in the UI or make the label optional.

What limits apply: maximum tag length (existing generic ones are at most 15 characters; the sketch uses 40) and maximum tags per closet (the sketch uses 50 for the column design; the table design would need a trigger or UI cap)?
How are migrations applied to the remote project (supabase db push by the developer)? No script or doc in the repo says. The client must tolerate the migration not being applied yet.

Are both the baseline ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES (baseline:718-741) and the 'not auto-exposed' behaviour described in config.toml:19-24 in force on remote? I could not verify; explicit grants make it moot.
Does regenerate_closet_passphrase exist on the remote DB? It is in no migration. It is out of scope for this request but would fail on any migration-built database.
Should supabase/schema.sql be touched? Commit 591ae6a updated it for a changed constraint; commit e1fee32 did not for a new table. For a new table I would leave it alone.

Do any production outfits carry labels outside the ten generic values (for example from direct DB edits)? If so, the backfill could also insert each closet's distinct in-use labels (SELECT DISTINCT closet_id, unnest(labels) FROM outfits ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) so nothing becomes unfilterable. I could not inspect remote data.

codeMaps.area: Accessibility conventions and Settings UI patterns for two new Settings sub-screens (Logs, Edit tags with add/remove) - iOS VoiceOver and web PWA screen reader/keyboard
codeMaps.summary:
SCOPE AND CONFIDENCE
Read-only mapping; nothing was built or run. Web/DOM claims were verified by reading react-native-web 0.21.2, @react-navigation/elements 2.9.38, @react-navigation/native-stack 7.18.8, @react-navigation/bottom-tabs 7.18.16 and expo-router 55.0.17 in node_modules. iOS/VoiceOver claims come from reading React Native 0.83.6 sources, not from a device - each is flagged "iPhone-only" below.

WHAT EXISTS TODAY
- Settings (/home/user/Zeeba/src/app/(tabs)/settings.tsx:19-110) is a single leaf tab screen: ScrollView root with aria-hidden={!isFocused} (:37-41), a centred 560px column (:116-124) of bordered cards (:125-130). Card titles are <Text role="heading" aria-level={2}> (:43, :61). Theme is View role="radiogroup" aria-label="Theme" containing Pressable role="radio" aria-checked (:65-93). Sign out is a bare Pressable role="button" named by its child text (:101-107). There are no navigation rows yet.
- Logs (/home/user/Zeeba/src/app/(tabs)/about.tsx:20-114) refetches on every focus and clears to a spinner each time (:34-55, :39), then renders spinner / error / empty / list (:57-107). A11y gaps: spinners unlabeled (:61, :85); error and empty text have no role (:67, :73, :79, :91); each entry is two sibling Texts with no list semantics (:96-105), i.e. two VoiceOver stops per entry.
- Web chrome: /home/user/Zeeba/src/components/AppShell.web.tsx wraps the router in skip link + header/nav + <main id="main-content" tabIndex=-1> + footer (:32-48). useAnnounceRouteChange (:71-98) runs on every pathname change after first render and focuses the first VISIBLE "h1, h2, [role=heading]" inside main (fallback: main).
- Page h1: tab pages get it from /home/user/Zeeba/src/components/HeaderBanner.web.tsx:30-36 (only rendered for the focused tab, (tabs)/_layout.web.tsx:26-27); nested stacks (closet, outfits) get it from react-navigation HeaderTitle, which renders role="heading" aria-level="1" (node_modules/@react-navigation/elements/lib/module/Header/HeaderTitle.js:15-18).
- Hidden screens on web: inactive tabs are display:none + aria-hidden ((tabs)/_layout.web.tsx:47-55); non-focused stack screens are display:none (node_modules/@react-navigation/native-stack/lib/module/views/NativeStackView.js:93-95) and aria-hidden (elements/lib/module/Screen.js:38).

(1) PROP CONVENTIONS
- Buttons: Pressable role="button"; name = visible child text; aria-label only for icon-only or per-item names. State is passed as BOTH disabled={x} and aria-disabled={x} (AddClothingItemForm.tsx:245-251, VoiceNotes.tsx:169-174); in-flight uses aria-busy (RemoveBackgroundButton.tsx:134). Per-item destructive precedent: aria-label={`Delete voice note by ${note.recorded_by}`} with visible "Delete" in theme.danger (VoiceNotes.tsx:372-379). Older files still use accessibilityRole/accessibilityLabel/accessibilityState (DeleteButton.tsx:24-26, EditButton.tsx:21-22, HeaderBackButton.tsx:23-24); README.md:76-80 and FilterPills.tsx:55-66 say to prefer role/aria-*. On web role="button" becomes a real <button type="button"> (react-native-web/dist/modules/AccessibilityUtil/propsToAccessibilityComponent.js:11-31; createDOMProps/index.js:834-836).
- Headings: h1 = page title only (HeaderBanner.web.tsx:31-32; native HeaderBanner.tsx:24 accessibilityRole="header"; stack header title). h2 = section/card titles (settings.tsx:43, :61). Everywhere else headings are level-less (index.tsx:96, :238; VoiceNotes.tsx:359; OutfitsGrid.tsx:77; ClosetHeader.tsx:18; NoAccessScreen.tsx:20) and on web a level-less heading renders as <h1> (propsToAccessibilityComponent.js:44-50).
- Lists: no role="list"/"listitem" anywhere; rows are plain Views (about.tsx:96-105, VoiceNotes.tsx:368-382). Row grouping precedent: View accessible aria-label={`${label}: ${value}`} (ClothingItemDetail.tsx:255-259). Counted section header precedent: aria-label={`${title}, ${count} ${noun}`} (ClosetHeader.tsx:15-23).
- Text inputs: the visible label is a sibling Text in a file-private Field (AddClothingItemForm.tsx:269-280), not programmatically associated; the TextInput carries aria-label={required ? `${label}, required` : label} (:320). Required is also a red " *" (:275). Styling: surfaceAlt fill, border token, textPrimary, placeholderTextColor={theme.textSecondary} (:306-313), minHeight 48 and fontSize 16 (:339-346). Web select uses aria-label + aria-required (NativeSelect.web.tsx:61-66). aria-invalid / aria-describedby are used nowhere. Validation errors are either a blocking showAlert('Missing information', ...) (AddClothingItemForm.tsx:84-86) or inline <Text role="alert"> (index.tsx:253-257).
- Radio groups: View role="radiogroup" aria-label + Pressable role="radio" aria-checked (settings.tsx:65-93; index.tsx:51-64, :107-118). Tabs: tablist + role="tab" aria-selected aria-label (FilterPills.tsx:30, :70-74).
- Links: expo-router <Link> (real <a href>) with aria-current="page" via a spread helper (HeaderNav.web.tsx:27-29, :57-70); Pressable role="link" for the skip link and external URLs (AppShell.web.tsx:110-118; ClothingItemDetail.tsx:263). In-app pushes from a control use role="button" + router.push (closet/index.tsx:79-83; OutfitsGrid.tsx:92-97) - the right precedent for the two new Settings buttons.
- Status/alert: Toast = always-mounted <Text role="alert" aria-live="polite"> on web (Toast.tsx:45-50). Progress = always-mounted <Text role="status" style={srOnly}> whose text toggles (VoiceNotes.tsx:191-193; RemoveBackgroundButton.tsx:153-157). Named spinners: <ActivityIndicator aria-label="Loading your closets" /> (index.tsx:101, :259), which is role="progressbar" on web.
- Visually hidden text: a local srOnly style {position:'absolute', width:1, height:1, overflow:'hidden', opacity:0}, duplicated in VoiceNotes.tsx:454-461 and RemoveBackgroundButton.tsx:202-208. Decorative content uses aria-hidden (VoiceNotes.tsx:187; NativeSelect.web.tsx:84).

(2) HOW RESULTS ARE ANNOUNCED
- Reuse: const { showToast } = useToast(); showToast('...'). Native calls AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility(text) (Toast.tsx:27-29); web changes the text of the always-mounted polite region (Toast.tsx:31, :45-52). ToastProvider wraps the whole app (src/app/_layout.tsx:17-23).
- Progress that must not be cut off on iOS: AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibilityWithOptions(text, { queue: true }) guarded by Platform.OS === 'ios' (RemoveBackgroundButton.tsx:166-172), plus a web-only role="status" region.
- Failures: showAlert("Couldn't ...", getErrorMessage(err, 'Something went wrong. Please try again.')) (VoiceNotes.tsx:350), which is Alert.alert on native and window.alert on web (src/utils/alert.ts:12-26).
- react-native-web's announceForAccessibility and setAccessibilityFocus are empty functions (react-native-web/dist/exports/AccessibilityInfo/index.js:75, :79), and announceForAccessibilityWithOptions / sendAccessibilityEvent do not exist there, so every native call must stay behind a Platform check.
- iOS ignores role="status"/"alert" and aria-live (no live regions); only AccessibilityInfo speaks.

(3) VOICEOVER AND A LIST OF REMOVABLE TAGS
- Name per button: aria-label={`Remove tag ${name}`} with visible text "Remove" (label-in-name holds), following VoiceNotes.tsx:375.
- Focus after removal: next row's Remove button; if the removed row was last, the previous row's; if the list is now empty, a non-input fallback (section heading or empty-state text with tabIndex={-1}). Do not use the text input as fallback: it opens the on-screen keyboard on the PWA.
- How to move focus: web -> ref.current.focus() (refs are DOM nodes). Native -> AccessibilityInfo.sendAccessibilityEvent(ref.current, 'focus'), the Fabric-aware path (react-native/Libraries/Components/AccessibilityInfo/AccessibilityInfo.js:449-459 -> Libraries/Renderer/implementations/ReactFabric-prod.js:10674-10686 -> React/Fabric/Mounting/RCTMountingManager.mm:218). AccessibilityInfo.setAccessibilityFocus(findNodeHandle(ref)) is the legacy route (AccessibilityInfo.js:442-444).
- This pattern does NOT exist in the repo: there is no findNodeHandle, setAccessibilityFocus or sendAccessibilityEvent in src; .focus( appears only in AppShell.web.tsx:15 and :96. The closest existing flow (voice-note delete, VoiceNotes.tsx:338-355) only toasts and lets focus drop.
- Sequence to implement: confirm -> await remove -> set state + remember the neighbour key -> in an effect after commit move focus -> then showToast(`Removed tag ${name}`). iPhone-only unknowns: whether a short delay is needed after Alert dismissal (UIKit restores VoiceOver focus to the element that opened the alert), and whether Toast's non-queued announcement is cut off by the focus-change speech.

(4) TARGETS, CONTRAST, DARK MODE
- Target size norm is 48: FilterPills.tsx:105, NativeSelect.tsx:123, NativeSelect.web.tsx:39, AddClothingItemForm.tsx:340, VoiceNotes.tsx:406 and :440-441 (minHeight and minWidth 48), RemoveBackgroundButton.tsx:180-181 (comment: 48pt, above the 44pt minimum). Primary/destructive buttons are 50 (AddClothingItemForm.tsx:374, DeleteButton.tsx:40, EditButton.tsx:32). Header icon buttons are a 28px icon plus hitSlop 8-10 (HeaderBackButton.tsx:25-27; closet/index.tsx:84-86).
- Existing Settings controls are under 44pt: theme segments use paddingVertical 10 with 15px text (settings.tsx:159-167). Do not copy that sizing.
- Tokens: /home/user/Zeeba/src/theme/theme.ts:18-81. I recomputed contrast: textPrimary, textSecondary, link and danger are all at least 5.0:1 on background, surface and surfaceAlt in both themes (worst case: dark danger on surfaceAlt 5.06:1). Failures: onStylist on stylist is 2.14:1 (white on #38bdf8); border on any surface is 1.3-1.7:1, so input boundaries rely on the surfaceAlt fill.
- Dark mode: const { theme, isDark } = useTheme() (ThemeContext.tsx:105-109); layout in StyleSheet.create, colours merged per render (settings.tsx:13-18, :31-34). Stack headers follow the theme through NavigationThemeProvider (theme.ts:89-104; src/app/_layout.tsx:31, :56). Web also syncs color-scheme (src/app/_layout.tsx:38-46).

(5) WEB PWA: FOCUS, BACK, H1
- Into a pushed sub-screen: no per-screen code is needed IF the navigation changes usePathname() and the new screen has a visible heading inside main - AppShell.web.tsx:71-98 focuses that heading. A Modal or in-place state swap would bypass this.
- After back (header control or browser back): the same hook focuses the first visible heading of the revealed screen, i.e. the h1 "Settings", not the button that was pressed. That is the app-wide convention. A screen-level attempt to restore focus to the trigger would be overridden, because the AppShell effect runs after child effects.
- Back control: detail routes use the shared /home/user/Zeeba/src/components/HeaderBackButton.tsx:21-28 -> a real <button aria-label="Back"> on web, 28x28 CSS px (hitSlop is a no-op on web). Nested stacks without headerLeft (closet/new, outfits/new) get react-navigation's default: on web an <a role="link" href> named "<previous title>, back" or "Go back" (elements/lib/module/Header/HeaderBackButton.js:27; PlatformPressable.js:107), icon-only 24x24; on iOS the system back button.
- The PWA manifest is display: standalone (/home/user/Zeeba/public/manifest.json:8), so there is no browser back button: the in-app back control is the only visible way back.
- Exactly one h1: true today on Settings (h1 + two h2) and Logs (h1 only). Not true on Home, Closet, Outfits or the detail pages, because of level-less headings. New screens must give every in-page heading an aria-level of 2 or more.
- document.title is never updated (expo-router/build/ExpoRoot.js:64-66 disables documentTitle; +html.tsx has no <title>) - pre-existing, out of scope.

(6) ACCESSIBLE CONFIRM-BEFORE-REMOVE
Use showAlert(title, message, [{ text: 'Cancel', style: 'cancel' }, { text: 'Remove', style: 'destructive', onPress }]) exactly as VoiceNotes.tsx:339-354 and useDeleteConfirm.ts:30-54 do.
- iOS: a UIAlertController; VoiceOver moves into it and reads title, message and buttons. The destructive style is visual only, so the button text must be the verb.
- Web: with two or more buttons it becomes window.confirm(`${title}\n\n${message}`), OK = first non-cancel button, Cancel = the cancel-styled one (alert.ts:28-34). Custom button labels are lost, so the message must be a complete question naming the tag and the consequence, e.g. title 'Remove tag', message 'Remove the tag "Casual"? ...'. It is a native browser dialog, read by screen readers; focus returns to the Remove button when it closes, and that button then unmounts - hence the focus move in (3).
- Playwright auto-dismisses dialogs unless a handler is registered, which makes confirm return false: every remove test needs page.once('dialog', d => d.accept()).

(7) ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
Proposed names (none exist in code yet; implementer and tests must agree): buttons "Logs" and "Edit tags"; h1 "Logs" and "Edit tags"; textbox "New tag"; button "Add tag"; list "Tags"; per-row button "Remove tag <name>"; button "Restore default tags"; spinners "Loading activity" / "Loading tags"; toasts "Added tag <name>", "Removed tag <name>", "Default tags restored".
Playwright prerequisites: (a) the web sign-in screen only offers Google unless EXPO_PUBLIC_ENABLE_TEST_AUTH=true (sign-in.tsx:35-81), and guest mode is native-only and in-memory (AuthContext.tsx:54, :77), so tests need a test-auth build or an injected session plus mocked Supabase REST; (b) use getByRole (ignores display:none screens) or :visible, never a bare locator('h1'); (c) axe-core is not installed; (d) preview-mode getActivityLog always returns [] (previewService.ts:403-405).

Settings
1. Two controls are real buttons: getByRole('button', {name:'Logs', exact:true}) and {name:'Edit tags'} are visible, tagName BUTTON, and the accessible name contains the visible text. iPhone-only: VoiceOver says "Logs, button" / "Edit tags, button" with no chevron or icon noise.
2. Heading outline: locator('main h1:visible') has count 1 ("Settings"); the card holding the new buttons has an h2 (getByRole('heading', {level:2})). iPhone-only: Headings rotor lists the same.
3. Keyboard: Tab reaches both; Enter and Space each navigate (assert URL). No element has a positive tabindex.
4. Target size: boundingBox height and width of each new button are at least 44 (repo norm 48) at 390x844 and 320x568.
5. Primary nav: getByRole('navigation', {name:'Primary'}).getByRole('link') is exactly Home, My Closet, Outfits, Settings; the Settings link has aria-current="page" on /settings and both sub-routes. iPhone-only: tab bar shows four tabs and VoiceOver says "Settings, tab, 4 of 4" (not "5 of 5").
6. Regression: radiogroup "Theme" still has three radios with exactly one aria-checked="true"; "Sign out" is still a button.

Navigation and focus (both sub-screens)
7. After activating either button the URL changes, exactly one h1 with the screen title is visible, and that h1 is focused (toBeFocused; document.activeElement is not BODY). iPhone-only: VoiceOver announces the new screen and the title has the header trait.
8. Exactly one visible back control, matched by getByRole('button', {name:/back/i}) or getByRole('link', {name:/back/i}); Enter activates it; at least 24x24 CSS px (target 44). iPhone-only: reads as a back button; two-finger scrub pops the screen.
9. After back via the control AND via page.goBack(): URL is /settings, h1 "Settings" is focused, and sub-screen controls are gone from the accessibility tree (getByRole('button', {name:'Add tag'}) has count 0). iPhone-only: VoiceOver focus is not lost.
10. Direct load / reload of each sub-route renders the screen with a working back control that lands on /settings.
11. While a sub-screen is open, getByRole('button', {name:'Sign out'}) has count 0 and Tab never reaches Settings-index controls.

Logs
12. Loading: with the activity request delayed via page.route, getByRole('progressbar', {name:'Loading activity'}) is visible. iPhone-only: label is spoken.
13. Error: with the request failing, getByRole('alert') containing the error text is visible; any retry affordance is a named button. iPhone-only: the error is spoken or is the first swipe after the title.
14. Empty: getByText('No activity yet.') is visible and not aria-hidden.
15. Populated: one getByRole('list') whose listitem count equals the mocked entry count; each item contains actor, action, item name and timestamp. iPhone-only: one swipe per entry, read as one phrase.
16. No "Logs" h1 exists while on other tabs, and /about behaves as decided (redirect or not-found) - assert whichever is chosen.

Edit tags - structure
17. locator('main h1:visible') has count 1 ("Edit tags"); every other heading has a level of 2 or more.
18. getByRole('textbox', {name:/new tag/i}) exists; computed font-size is at least 16px; height at least 44; a visible label with the same words is present.
19. getByRole('button', {name:'Add tag'}) is enabled even when the input is empty (never natively disabled).
20. getByRole('list', {name:'Tags'}) has one listitem per tag (10 defaults on first use); each listitem has exactly one button named "Remove tag <name>"; all names are unique.
21. Each Remove button is at least 44x44 and its visible text is contained in its accessible name.

Edit tags - add
22. Add by button: fill "Vintage", click Add -> the listitem and "Remove tag Vintage" appear, the input is empty, locator('[role="alert"][aria-live="polite"]') contains "Vintage", and activeElement is not BODY. iPhone-only: the confirmation is spoken in full.
23. Add by Enter: type and press Enter -> tag added, input still focused and empty.
24. Empty or whitespace-only: list count unchanged; a visible error is exposed with role="alert"; the input has aria-invalid="true" and aria-describedby equal to the error element's id; focus is on the input. iPhone-only: the error is spoken.
25. Duplicate (case- and whitespace-insensitive, e.g. "casual " when "Casual" exists): same assertions as 24, and the message names the duplicate.
26. Too long: an error stating the limit, same assertions as 24. If the input is hard-capped with maxLength instead, the limit must be visible text associated through aria-describedby and typed text must be capped (check with pressSequentially).
27. Recovery: after a successful add or after editing the text, the error is gone and aria-invalid is absent.
28. Triggering the same error twice still ends with focus on the input and aria-describedby set. That it is re-spoken is iPhone/screen-reader-only.
