conventions: Use role and aria-* props on new code (role='button', aria-label, aria-checked, aria-selected, aria-busy, aria-hidden), not accessibilityRole/accessibilityLabel/accessibilityState: README.md:76-80 and FilterPills.tsx:55-66 say so, and react-native-web 0.21 does not map accessibilityState at all. accessibilityHint is the one legacy prop still used on purpose, for iOS-only extra context (RemoveBackgroundButton.tsx:135-139, sign-in.tsx:102).

Buttons are Pressable role='button'. The accessible name is the visible child text; add aria-label only for icon-only buttons or per-item names, and it must contain the visible text (RemoveBackgroundButton.tsx:46-48). Per-item template is verb + thing + identifier, e.g. 'Delete voice note by Ava' (VoiceNotes.tsx:375) -> 'Remove tag Casual'.
A control that pushes a screen is a button with router.push (closet/index.tsx:79-83, OutfitsGrid.tsx:92-97), not a Link.

Every heading needs role='heading' AND aria-level. h1 comes only from the navigator header (HeaderBanner.web.tsx:31-32 or the stack header title); card and section titles are aria-level={2} (settings.tsx:43, :61).

Tab-root screens put aria-hidden={!isFocused} on their root container using useIsFocused from expo-router, with the standard comment pointing at src/app/(tabs)/index.tsx (settings.tsx:20-23, :40; about.tsx:21-24, :110).

Colours come only from useTheme() tokens; static layout lives in StyleSheet.create and colour objects are merged at render (settings.tsx:13-18, :31-34). Destructive text is theme.danger, secondary text theme.textSecondary, cards theme.surface with theme.border, inputs theme.surfaceAlt.

Settings layout: container width 100%, maxWidth 560, alignSelf center, paddingHorizontal 16, paddingTop 24, paddingBottom 40, gap 16; cards borderWidth 1, borderRadius 10, padding 16, gap 12; card title 16px weight 600 (settings.tsx:116-134).

Touch targets use minHeight 48 (and minWidth 48 for compact buttons), never a fixed height, so Dynamic Type can grow them (VoiceNotes.tsx:405-411, :439-445; FilterPills.tsx:104-111). hitSlop is only a native extra.

Text inputs: aria-label on the TextInput (append ', required' when required), a visible label Text above it, minHeight 48, fontSize 16, borderWidth 1, borderRadius 10, placeholderTextColor={theme.textSecondary}, maxLength where relevant (AddClothingItemForm.tsx:294-324, :339-346). Forms sit in a ScrollView with keyboardShouldPersistTaps='handled' (AddClothingItemForm.tsx:141).

Success is announced with useToast().showToast('short past-tense phrase, no full stop') (VoiceNotes.tsx:328, :348). Failures use showAlert with a title starting Couldn't and getErrorMessage(err, 'Something went wrong. Please try again.') (VoiceNotes.tsx:350).

Destructive actions confirm through showAlert(title, question, [{ text: 'Cancel', style: 'cancel' }, { text: '<Verb>', style: 'destructive', onPress }]) (VoiceNotes.tsx:339-354, useDeleteConfirm.ts:30-54).

A button that may hold focus while work is in flight is not disabled: keep it pressable, early-return in the handler, set aria-busy and change its label (RemoveBackgroundButton.tsx:83-89, :128-134). Where disabled is used, pass disabled and aria-disabled together (AddClothingItemForm.tsx:247-251).
Spinners that stand alone get an aria-label describing what is loading (index.tsx:101, :259), inside a centred flex container (about.tsx:120-124).

Web-only progress text uses an always-mounted <Text role='status'> with the local srOnly style whose content toggles between '' and the message (VoiceNotes.tsx:191-193); native announcements go through AccessibilityInfo behind a Platform.OS check (RemoveBackgroundButton.tsx:166-172).
Data loading uses the cancelled-flag pattern inside useFocusEffect(useCallback(...)) with getErrorMessage for the fallback string (about.tsx:34-55).

gotchas: Disabled Pressable loses focus on web: with role='button' it renders <button>, and disabled adds tabIndex -1, aria-disabled and the native disabled attribute (react-native-web Pressable/index.js:118-133; createDOMProps/index.js:155, :314-320). If the Add button is disabled when the input empties after a successful add, the focused button drops focus to <body>. Keep Add and Remove buttons enabled and validate on press.

aria-disabled without disabled is silently dropped on a web Pressable: Pressable writes 'aria-disabled': disabled after spreading the rest props (Pressable/index.js:124-125), so there is no way to get aria-disabled='true' on a focusable <button> through Pressable. Use aria-busy plus an early return.

A heading without aria-level becomes an extra <h1> on web (propsToAccessibilityComponent.js:44-50). useAnnounceRouteChange focuses the first visible h1/h2/[role=heading], so a stray level-less heading can also steal route-change focus.

Hiding the Logs tab with href: null leaves the route in the tab list (expo-router TabsClient.js:16-43), and on iOS each tab's label is built as 'label, tab, i of routes.length' (bottom-tabs BottomTabBar.js:293). VoiceOver would then say 'Settings, tab, 5 of 5' with four visible tabs. Move the file out of the (tabs) route list instead, or set tabBarAccessibilityLabel on every tab.

useAnnounceRouteChange only fires when usePathname() changes and needs a visible heading in main (AppShell.web.tsx:71-98). A Modal or in-place state swap for Logs/Edit tags gets no focus move; autoFocus on an input in a pushed screen is overridden by it; any screen-level focus restore after back is overridden by it.

In a nested stack the default web back control is a link named '<previous screen title>, back' (elements HeaderBackButton.js:27, PlatformPressable.js:107). If the index screen has no title option the name becomes 'index, back' and iOS shows 'index' as the back title. It is icon-only 24x24 on web.
hitSlop does nothing on web (not forwarded by react-native-web View or Pressable), so the shared HeaderBackButton is 28x28 CSS px there (HeaderBackButton.tsx:25-27).

accessibilityHint, accessibilityValue, accessibilityState and accessibilityViewIsModal are not forwarded by react-native-web (dist/modules/forwardedProps/index.js lists none of them). They are iOS/Android-only.

On web AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility and setAccessibilityFocus are no-ops, and announceForAccessibilityWithOptions and sendAccessibilityEvent are undefined (react-native-web AccessibilityInfo/index.js:35-93) - calling the last two on web throws. Branch on Platform.OS.

Toast does not re-announce an identical consecutive message on web: the text node does not change (Toast.tsx:31) and the message is never cleared, only faded (Toast.tsx:34-36). Include the tag name in every toast so consecutive messages differ.

Toast uses the non-queued announceForAccessibility on iOS (Toast.tsx:27-29). Moving VoiceOver focus at the same moment may cut the announcement off; RemoveBackgroundButton uses the queued variant for that reason (:166-172). Needs a real iPhone to confirm.

An inline role='alert' that stays mounted with unchanged text is not re-announced on web when the same validation error happens twice. Return focus to the input and link the error with aria-describedby so it is read on focus.

iOS ignores aria-invalid, aria-describedby, aria-required, aria-level, aria-current and aria-live: native View only maps the props listed in react-native/Libraries/Components/View/View.js:34-46. Errors must be spoken with AccessibilityInfo on native (or carried in accessibilityHint).

On iOS an accessible parent's label is the comma-joined labels of all its subviews and does not skip aria-hidden children (RCTViewComponentView.mm:1338-1358). A row button with a visible chevron or icon glyph needs an explicit aria-label or VoiceOver reads the glyph.
aria-atomic passed as 'aria-atomic' is dropped by a react-native-web bug (createDOMProps/index.js:180 reads the wrong variable). Do not design a live region that depends on it.

Do not put role='list' on a ScrollView: the role lands on the outer element with a content wrapper between it and the items (ul > div > li). Put it on a plain inner View. role='form' renders a real <form> and role='region' a <section> (propsToAccessibilityComponent.js:11-31).
react-native-web TextInput blurs on Enter unless blurOnSubmit={false} (TextInput/index.js:270-293); it does not read submitBehavior. Without it, add-by-Enter drops focus out of the input.

TextInput font size must be at least 16px on the PWA or iOS Safari zooms the page on focus (general iOS Safari behaviour, not verified here). The Home modal input (index.tsx:356-361) sets no font size - do not copy it.

window.confirm discards custom button labels on web (alert.ts:28-34): the question text alone must name the tag and the consequence. Playwright auto-dismisses dialogs when no handler is registered, so an unhandled remove test silently cancels.
The PWA runs display: standalone (public/manifest.json:8): there is no browser back button, so a sub-screen without a header back control is a dead end.

Stylist-mode stack headers are white on #38bdf8 = 2.14:1 ((tabs)/closet/_layout.tsx:18-19; theme.ts:63-64). Copying that header styling to a Settings stack puts the Logs/Edit tags title and back control below AA while in stylist mode.

designs.name: Smallest correct change: Settings becomes a nested stack (index / logs / tags); tags live in a closets.outfit_labels text[] column edited by the owner through two atomic invoker RPCs

decisions.tagOwnership: A tag list belongs to a CLOSET, stored on its closets row. Reason: outfits, the filter pills and the create-outfit form are already scoped to activeClosetId (src/components/OutfitsGrid.tsx:36, src/components/CreateOutfitForm.tsx:72,187), and stylists create outfits in the owner's closet (RLS "Members can manage outfits", baseline_schema.sql:379), so they must see the owner's list, not their own. A user owns one closet (getOwnCloset uses maybeSingle, src/services/supabaseClosetsService.ts:31-39), so "my tags" and "my closet's tags" are the same thing for the person editing.
decisions.whoCanEdit: Owner only. Reason: the existing policy "Owners can update their closets" (baseline_schema.sql:403) already enforces exactly this with no new policy, and the request says a user creates "their own" tags. Settings > Edit tags follows the ACTIVE closet, like every other closet-scoped screen: in My Closet mode it edits the user's own closet; in Stylist mode it shows the selected closet's tags READ-ONLY (no input, no Add, no Remove buttons in the tree) with the sentence "Only the closet owner can add or remove tags. To edit your own tags, switch to My Closet on the Home tab." Reason for not editing the own closet while in stylist mode: ClosetContext only loads myCloset while closetMode === 'my-closet' (src/context/ClosetContext.tsx:51-75) and keeps a stale value otherwise (it survives sign-out/sign-in because ClosetProvider sits above the Stack, src/app/_layout.tsx:62), so that path would need a second own-closet loader. Guests (preview mode) own the preview closet and can edit in memory.
decisions.storage: One new column: closets.outfit_labels text[] NOT NULL, DEFAULT = the ten generic tags, plus a count CHECK (<= 50). No new table, no trigger, no new policy, no new table grant. Reasons: (1) the DEFAULT is both the backfill for existing closets and the seed for new ones, because the app insert (supabaseClosetsService.ts:49-53) and supabase/seed.sql:75-84 both omit the column; (2) existing closets RLS already gives members SELECT (:387) and owners UPDATE (:403); (3) the list rides on the closet row that ClosetContext already loads, so the UI needs no second request and no extra loading/error state. Writes do NOT overwrite the array from the client: two invoker (non SECURITY DEFINER) RPCs, add_closet_outfit_label and remove_closet_outfit_label, change one element under a row lock and return the whole saved list - the same pattern and reasoning as increment_outfit_compliment_count (20260722025112). That is what prevents a phone holding yesterday's list from silently dropping a tag added on another device.
decisions.removalSemantics: Removing a tag removes it from the closet's list only. outfits.labels is never rewritten, so no outfit loses data: an outfit that carried the tag keeps the string, still appears under All, and gets its pill back if the same tag is added again (filter matching becomes case-insensitive so re-adding in a different case also works). Reason for not stripping: any UPDATE with labels in the SET list fires log_outfit_activity_trigger (20260717025406:141-143) and bumps updated_at (20260722040000:31-33), which would spam Logs and raise ConflictError for anyone with those outfits open. Effects in the UI: the pill disappears from the Outfits filter row and the option disappears from the create-outfit Tag select immediately (both read activeClosetLabels from context). A filter selection or a half-filled create form pointing at the removed tag falls back to All / unselected by derivation (no effect, no stale submit). Removal is confirmed first (showAlert, VoiceNotes.tsx:339-354 pattern) and the confirm text states the consequence. Remove is idempotent on the server.
decisions.emptyListBehaviour: Allowed - the user may remove every tag ("add remove as they want"). Outfits tab: the FilterPills row is not rendered at all when the list is empty (precedent: ClosetList.tsx:32-39), every outfit is shown. Create outfit: the Tag select is replaced by explanatory text and the tag is no longer required; the outfit is saved with labels: [] (the column default is already '{}', baseline_schema.sql:182). Copy, My Closet mode: "You have no tags yet. Add some in Settings > Edit tags, or save this outfit without one." Stylist mode: "This closet has no tags yet, so this outfit will be saved without one." When the list is non-empty the tag stays required exactly as today. Edit tags screen shows "No tags yet. Add one above." (owner) or "This closet has no tags yet." (stylist) and Add keeps working.

designs.a11ySpec:
Conventions used throughout: role / aria-* props (README.md:76-80), never accessibilityState; every in-page heading has an explicit aria-level of 2 (a level-less heading becomes a second h1 on web); h1 comes only from the stack header title; buttons are never disabled; no Modal is used (so the web route announcer and focus hiding keep working). "iOS" below means native VoiceOver; "web" means the PWA/browser with VoiceOver, NVDA or keyboard. iOS behaviour is derived from React Native 0.83 source and repo precedent - it could not be run here.

## A. Tab bar and primary nav
- iOS/Android tab bar: four tabs - Home, My Closet, Outfits, Settings. VoiceOver: "Settings, tab, 4 of 4". No hidden fifth route exists, so the count is right.
- Web: nav landmark "Primary" contains exactly four links (Home, My Closet, Outfits, Settings). The Settings link carries aria-current="page" on /settings, /settings/logs and /settings/tags.

## B. Settings root (/settings)
- Page title: stack header "Settings". Web: h1 (react-navigation HeaderTitle renders role=heading aria-level=1). iOS: navigation bar title with the header trait.
- Card heading "Closet": Text role="heading" aria-level={2}. Web: h2. iOS: heading in the rotor.
- "Logs" button: Pressable role="button" aria-label="Logs", visible text "Logs" plus a decorative "›" (aria-hidden). Web: real <button>, name "Logs", Tab-reachable, Enter/Space activate. iOS: "Logs, button" (the explicit label stops VoiceOver appending the chevron). minHeight 48.
- "Edit tags" button: same, aria-label="Edit tags". iOS: "Edit tags, button".
- Activation: router.push. iOS posts the screen-changed notification itself; VoiceOver lands on the new screen. Web: the pathname changes, so AppShell.web.tsx:71-98 moves focus to the first visible heading - the new screen's h1 ("Logs" / "Edit tags") - which is announced by name.
- Unchanged: radiogroup "Theme" with three radios (aria-checked), "Sign out" button.
- While a sub-screen is open the root is display:none + aria-hidden on web (stack + screen root aria-hidden={!isFocused}); its buttons are out of the tab order and the accessibility tree.

## C. Back control on Logs and Edit tags (default stack header, no custom headerLeft)
- iOS: system back button titled "Settings" - VoiceOver "Settings, back button"; the two-finger scrub (escape) gesture pops the screen.
- Web/PWA: react-navigation's header back control, a link named "Settings, back" (previous screen title + ", back"), Tab-reachable, Enter activates. In the installed PWA (display: standalone, no browser chrome) this is the visible way back.
- After back (control, browser Back or scrub): iOS announces the Settings screen; web focuses the h1 "Settings" (route announcer). Focus is intentionally not restored to the pressed row - that is the app-wide convention.
- Cold load / reload of /settings/logs or /settings/tags: unstable_settings.initialRouteName = 'index' puts Settings underneath, so the back control exists and lands on /settings (same mechanism as /closet/new; to be confirmed on the exported build).

## D. Logs screen (/settings/logs) - no interactive elements besides the header
- h1 "Logs" (header). Exactly one h1; no other headings.
- Loading: ActivityIndicator aria-label="Loading activity". Web: role=progressbar named "Loading activity". iOS: "Loading activity".
- Errors: Text role="alert" (web announces on insert; iOS reads it as the first element after the title).
- Empty: plain text "No activity yet."
- List: View role="list" (web <ul>) containing one View role="listitem" accessible per entry (web <li>). iOS: one swipe per entry, read as "Ava created outfit Sunday Brunch, 11/11/2026, 10:00 AM". Web: list with N items; each item's two text lines are read in order.

## E. Edit tags screen (/settings/tags)
- h1 "Edit tags" (header). h2 "Add a tag" (owner only). h2 with visible text "Tags (N)" and aria-label "Tags, N tags" / "Tags, 1 tag". No other headings.
- Loading: ActivityIndicator aria-label="Loading tags". Closet error: Text role="alert".
- Text field: TextInput aria-label="New tag", visible label "New tag" above it, visible hint "Up to 30 characters.", maxLength 30, fontSize 16 (no iOS Safari zoom), minHeight 48. Web: textbox "New tag"; Enter submits and focus stays in the field (blurOnSubmit={false}). iOS: "New tag, text field"; the Done key submits and keeps the field active (submitBehavior="submit").
- "Add tag" button: Pressable role="button", name from visible text "Add tag", aria-busy={true} while saving, never disabled (a second press while busy is ignored). Web: <button>. iOS: "Add tag, button". keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled" so one double-tap works with the keyboard open.
  - Success: field cleared, focus stays where it was (field or button), toast "Added tag <name>". The new tag is the last list item.
  - Any failure, including validation (empty, duplicate, limit, not owner, network): showAlert("Couldn't add tag", <sentence>). iOS: UIAlertController - VoiceOver moves into it and reads title, message and OK. Web: window.alert, read by screen readers. On dismissal focus returns to the element that triggered it. Chosen over inline errors because iOS ignores aria-invalid/aria-describedby/role=alert.
- Tag list: View role="list" (web <ul>) with one View role="listitem" (<li>) per tag: the tag text, then (owner only) the Remove button. iOS: two stops per row - "Casual", then "Remove tag Casual, button".
- Remove button (one per tag, owner only): Pressable role="button", aria-label={`Remove tag ${label}`}, visible text "Remove" in theme.danger (label-in-name holds), aria-busy while that tag is being removed, minHeight 48 and minWidth 48, never disabled.
  - Press: confirm via showAlert('Remove tag', 'Remove the tag "<name>"? Outfits that already use it keep it and still appear under All, but it will no longer be a filter or a choice for new outfits.', [Cancel (cancel), Remove (destructive)]). iOS: alert with buttons "Cancel" and "Remove". Web: window.confirm showing title + message (button labels are the browser's OK/Cancel, which is why the question names the tag and the consequence).
  - Cancel: nothing changes, no toast, focus returns to the same Remove button.
  - Confirm, success: the row disappears; focus moves to the NEXT row's Remove button; if the removed row was last, to the PREVIOUS row's; if the list is now empty, to the h2 "Tags, 0 tags" (never to the text field - that would open the on-screen keyboard). Web: element.focus() (tabIndex -1 is set on the heading first). iOS/Android: AccessibilityInfo.sendAccessibilityEvent(node, 'focus'). Then the toast "Removed tag <name>". document.activeElement is never <body> afterwards.
  - Confirm, failure: showAlert("Couldn't remove tag", ...); the list is unchanged; focus returns to the Remove button.
- Stylist mode (read-only): the field, "Add tag" and all Remove buttons are not rendered at all (nothing disabled or hidden-but-focusable); the first text explains why and how to edit your own tags.
- Empty list: sentence "No tags yet. Add one above." / "This closet has no tags yet."; no empty list element is rendered.

## F. Toast announcements (components/Toast.tsx)
- Web: the always-mounted Text role="alert" aria-live="polite" gets the new text; polite, so it is spoken after the focus announcement. Every message contains the tag name, so consecutive toasts differ and are re-announced.
- iOS: AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibilityWithOptions(text, { queue: true }) - queued behind the speech for the newly focused element instead of being cut off by it. Android: announceForAccessibility (unchanged).

## G. Outfits tab and Create outfit
- Filter pills: unchanged semantics (tablist; each pill role="tab" aria-label=<tag> aria-selected). The accessible name is now exactly the visible text (the capitalize transform is gone). With zero tags the row is absent. If the selected tag is removed, "All" is the selected tab again - never a state with no selected tab.
- Create outfit Tag field: web <select aria-label="Tag" aria-required="true"> with the disabled placeholder "Select a tag" and one option per tag, text verbatim. iOS: button "Tag, required", value "<tag>" or "Not selected", hint "Double tap to change selection"; opens the native action sheet titled "Tag". With zero tags: no control, just the explanatory sentence, and "Save outfit" is enabled once the other required fields are filled.

## H. Sizes, contrast, text size
- New targets are at least 48 high (rows, Add, Remove, field); the header back control is react-navigation's default, as on /closet/new today.
- Text uses textPrimary / textSecondary / danger on surface or background and onAccent on accent - all at least 4.5:1 in both themes (theme.ts:51-81). The Settings stack header is always surface/textPrimary, so its titles never sit on the low-contrast stylist blue.
- All heights are minHeight, tag text wraps (flex: 1) and Remove keeps its own width, so large Dynamic Type and a 320 px viewport reflow without clipping or horizontal scroll.

## I. Checks that need a real iPhone (cannot be done here)
(1) VoiceOver focus lands on the neighbouring Remove button after the confirm alert is dismissed (UIKit first returns focus to the pressed button; if the move does not stick, defer moveFocusTo by one frame). (2) "Removed tag <name>" is spoken in full after the focus announcement. (3) window.confirm and the live-region toast are read by VoiceOver in the installed standalone PWA. (4) "Settings, tab, 4 of 4".

-- FILE: supabase/migrations/20261111000000_closet_outfit_labels.sql
-- (sorts after 20261013000000_voice_notes.sql)

-- Per-closet outfit labels - what the app's UI calls "tags". Until now the
-- list was a constant compiled into the app (OUTFIT_LABELS in
-- src/services/dataService.types.ts). This table lets each closet owner add
-- their own and remove the ones they don't use (Settings > Edit tags); the
-- Outfits filter pills and the create-outfit form read it.
--
-- One row per label, not a text[] column on closets, because:
--   * two devices adding or removing different labels become independent
--     single-row INSERTs/DELETEs that cannot overwrite each other. A client
--     that rewrote a whole array would be last-write-wins, and closets has no
--     updated_at token to detect that;
--   * "no two labels that differ only by letter case" is a unique index and
--     the length/whitespace rules are plain CHECKs, so they hold for every
--     writer, not just for this version of the app;
--   * the feature never needs UPDATE on closets, the row that also holds
--     owner_id and pass_phrase.
--
-- Who can do what: every member of a closet (owner and stylists) can read its
-- labels - stylists create outfits in the owner's closet and must pick from
-- the owner's list. Only the owner can add or remove. There is deliberately
-- no UPDATE policy: labels are added and removed, never renamed, so a row can
-- never be re-pointed at another closet.
--
-- outfits.labels stays free text and is NOT tied to this table (no foreign
-- key, no trigger, nothing rewritten when a label is removed). App builds
-- released before this migration keep writing the ten original strings, and
-- rewriting outfits would log an "edited" activity row and bump updated_at
-- (the optimistic-concurrency token) for every outfit touched. An outfit
-- whose label is no longer in the list simply matches no filter pill; it
-- still shows under "All", and matches again if the label is re-added.
--
-- The ten starter labels below are mirrored in
-- src/services/dataService.types.ts (DEFAULT_OUTFIT_LABELS), and the limits
-- (30 characters, 50 labels per closet) in MAX_OUTFIT_LABEL_LENGTH and
-- MAX_OUTFIT_LABELS_PER_CLOSET.

-- Every new closet starts with the ten generic labels. SECURITY DEFINER
-- because this runs inside whatever statement inserted the closet: the INSERT
-- policy above checks ownership through auth.uid(), which is NULL for
-- seed.sql and service-role inserts, and the starter labels must not depend
-- on who created the closet. It only ever writes labels for the closet row
-- that was just inserted (NEW.id), so it cannot be aimed at another closet.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."seed_closet_outfit_labels"() RETURNS "trigger"
    LANGUAGE "plpgsql" SECURITY DEFINER
    SET "search_path" TO 'public'
    AS $$
begin
  insert into public.closet_outfit_labels (closet_id, name, sort_order)
  select new.id, d.name, d.ord::integer
  from unnest(array[
    'Girly/Romantic', 'Work', 'Casual', 'Date Night', 'Athleisure',
    'Formal Event', 'Street Style', 'Minimalist Chic', 'Artsy', 'Boho'
  ]) with ordinality as d(name, ord)
  on conflict do nothing;

  return new;
end;
$$;

GRANT ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."seed_closet_outfit_labels"() TO "authenticated";
GRANT ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."seed_closet_outfit_labels"() TO "service_role";

-- migration runs is seeded by one path or the other; ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
-- makes the two paths safe to overlap.

    AFTER INSERT ON "public"."closets"
    FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION "public"."seed_closet_outfit_labels"();


-- Backfill 1: every existing closet gets the same ten starter labels, in the
-- order the app has always shown them.
INSERT INTO "public"."closet_outfit_labels" ("closet_id", "name", "sort_order")
SELECT "c"."id", "d"."name", ("d"."ord")::integer
FROM "public"."closets" "c"
CROSS JOIN "unnest"(ARRAY['Girly/Romantic'::"text", 'Work'::"text", 'Casual'::"text", 'Date Night'::"text", 'Athleisure'::"text", 'Formal Event'::"text", 'Street Style'::"text", 'Minimalist Chic'::"text", 'Artsy'::"text", 'Boho'::"text"]) WITH ORDINALITY AS "d"("name", "ord")
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;


-- Backfill 2 (safety net): any label already in use on a closet's outfits
-- that is not one of the ten - e.g. from a manual edit - is added to that
-- closet's list, so no existing outfit loses its filter pill because of this
-- migration. Only values that satisfy the CHECKs above are taken, so this
-- cannot fail on unexpected data; anything else stays on its outfit and
-- shows under "All". outfits is only read here, never written.
INSERT INTO "public"."closet_outfit_labels" ("closet_id", "name")
SELECT DISTINCT "o"."closet_id", "btrim"("l"."name")
FROM "public"."outfits" "o"
CROSS JOIN LATERAL "unnest"("o"."labels") AS "l"("name")
WHERE "l"."name" IS NOT NULL
  AND "char_length"("btrim"("l"."name")) BETWEEN 1 AND 30
  AND "btrim"("l"."name") !~ '^\s|\s$|\s\s|[[:cntrl:]]'
  AND "lower"("btrim"("l"."name")) <> 'all'
ORDER BY 1, 2
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;


-- Caps a closet at 50 labels. The app checks this too, but a CHECK cannot
-- count rows and the Data API would otherwise let an owner insert without
-- limit - and stylists load this list on every Outfits visit. AFTER INSERT,
-- so it only runs for rows that already passed RLS and the constraints.
-- The row lock serialises label inserts per closet so two devices adding at
-- the same moment cannot both see 49; NO KEY UPDATE does not block the
-- KEY SHARE lock that foreign-key checks take, so creating outfits or items
-- in the same closet is unaffected. SECURITY DEFINER so the lock and the
-- count are exact whatever the caller's own access to closets is.
-- Created after the backfills so it cannot abort them.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."enforce_closet_outfit_label_limit"() RETURNS "trigger"
    LANGUAGE "plpgsql" SECURITY DEFINER
    SET "search_path" TO 'public'
    AS $$
declare
  v_count integer;
begin
  perform 1 from public.closets where id = new.closet_id for no key update;

  select count(*) into v_count
  from public.closet_outfit_labels
  where closet_id = new.closet_id;

  if v_count > 50 then
    raise exception 'A closet can have at most 50 tags';
  end if;

  return null;
end;
$$;

risks: Deploy order: the migration must be applied to the remote database before, or together with, the client release. It cannot be applied or inspected from this environment. If the web client ships first, the grid and the create form fall back to the ten defaults, but Edit tags shows a load error until the table exists.

The SQL is correct by inspection only. It must be exercised (PGlite with stubs, check list at the end of migrationSql) before it is run on production: the regex CHECK, WITH ORDINALITY, FOR NO KEY UPDATE inside a trigger, and ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING against an expression index.

Atomicity depends on the migration runner executing the file in one transaction, which I could not verify for this project. The statement order is safe if it does not (seed trigger before backfill, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING), but a failure half-way through a non-transactional run would need manual cleanup before re-running, because CREATE TABLE and CREATE POLICY are run-once by repo convention.

Already-installed iOS builds keep the hardcoded ten tags and ignore the owner's list. They can still create outfits with a tag the owner removed, and they show no pill for custom tags. This is tolerated by design (outfits.labels stays free text) and ends when users update.

A stylist can still save an outfit with a just-removed tag if the owner removes it in the instant between the form's pre-save re-check and the insert. The outfit then behaves like a legacy-tagged one (visible under All). Closing this fully needs a server-side check on outfits, which would break old builds.

An existing outfit cannot be re-tagged: the edit-outfit form does not edit labels (pre-existing, UpdateOutfitInput at src/services/dataService.types.ts:323-326). Outfits whose tag was removed, or that were created while the closet had no tags, are reachable only under All unless the same tag name is re-added. Adding a tag field to the edit form was not requested and is left out.

iOS VoiceOver cannot be run here. Unverified on a device: the 500 ms delay before moving focus after the confirm alert closes, whether the queued toast announcement is heard after the focus change, and how role list/listitem Views read. The shared Toast change (queued announcements on iOS) affects every screen that toasts.

Case-insensitive uniqueness is decided by Postgres lower() and by JavaScript toLowerCase() on the client. decisions.tagOwnership: A tag list belongs to a CLOSET, stored on the closets row. Reason: outfits live in closets and stylists create outfits in the owner's closet (RLS "Members can manage outfits", supabase/migrations/20260101000000_baseline_schema.sql:379; CreateOutfitForm writes to activeClosetId, src/components/CreateOutfitForm.tsx:72,187), so owner and stylist must see the same list or the filter pills would disagree about the same outfits. A user owns exactly one closet (getOwnCloset uses maybeSingle, src/services/supabaseClosetsService.ts:31-39), so "my tags" and "my closet's tags" are the same thing to the user. Naming: UI copy says "tag"; code and DB keep "label" (outfits.labels, Outfit.labels, closets.outfit_labels) so nothing existing is renamed.
decisions.whoCanEdit: Owner only. Stylists read the owner's list (filter pills and the create-outfit Tag select) but cannot change it. Settings > Edit tags ALWAYS edits the signed-in user's OWN closet, including while the Home toggle is on Stylist; the screen says so in text ("These tags belong to your closet, <name>. Stylists on your closet use the same list."). A user with no closet of their own (pure stylist) gets an explanatory empty state and no form. Reason: Settings is personal and the request says "their own custom tags"; RLS already restricts closets UPDATE to the owner (baseline:403), so no new policy and no SECURITY DEFINER is needed. Because ClosetContext only loads the own closet in my-closet mode (src/context/ClosetContext.tsx:51-75), the Edit tags screen fetches it itself with dataService.getOwnCloset(userId) on focus (same approach as src/components/outfitDetailPage.tsx:81) and pushes results into the context cache with applyClosetLabels.
decisions.storage: One new column: closets.outfit_labels text[] NOT NULL, DEFAULT = the ten current labels, plus a CHECK constraint backed by an IMMUTABLE validator function and two invoker-rights RPCs (add_closet_outfit_label, remove_closet_outfit_label) that each return the full updated list. Reasons: (1) the column default backfills every existing closet and seeds every new one (the app's plain INSERT at supabaseClosetsService.ts:48-56 and supabase/seed.sql:75-84 omit the column) with no trigger and no backfill statement; (2) existing closets policies already give members SELECT (baseline:387) and owners UPDATE (baseline:403); (3) the list arrives with the closet row the app already loads, so the Outfits filter and create form have no second request and no extra loading state to announce. RPCs instead of a client-side whole-array UPDATE so two devices cannot overwrite each other with a stale copy (closets has no updated_at; src/services/occConcurrency.ts:5 covers only outfits and clothing_items). A separate table was rejected: it needs a seeding trigger, a backfill, its own RLS, a sort column and a second fetch, and buys nothing once editing is owner-only.
decisions.removalSemantics: Removing a tag removes it from closets.outfit_labels only. outfits.labels is NOT rewritten: an UPDATE naming labels fires log_outfit_activity_trigger (supabase/migrations/20260717025406_create_activity_tablejlzv.sql:141-143) and bumps updated_at (20260722040000:31-33), which would spam Logs and throw ConflictError at anyone with that outfit open. Effects: the tag's filter pill and its option in the create-outfit select disappear immediately (context update); outfits that carry it stay visible under All and match again if the identical tag is added back; if the removed tag was the selected filter, OutfitsGrid resets to All; if it was selected in an open create form, the select resets to its placeholder. Because nothing is destroyed, there is NO confirm dialog: the row stays in the list as "<name> (removed)" and its button becomes Undo (re-adds the same string at the same position via target_position). The removed row disappears the next time the screen gains focus. No activity_logs entry is written for tag edits (item_type is CHECK-limited and the client throws on unknown values, src/services/dataService.types.ts:248-251). No "Restore default tags" button: not requested, Undo covers slips, and retyping a default restores it.

designs.a11ySpec:
Principles: (1) navigation is a real route push, so iOS posts its screen-change notification and the web shell's useAnnounceRouteChange (src/components/AppShell.web.tsx:71-98) focuses the new page's h1; (2) no control that can hold focus is ever disabled or unmounted by its own action, so focus is never lost and no programmatic VoiceOver focus calls are needed; (3) every outcome is spoken: Toast = queued announcement on iOS / polite live region on web, validation = role="alert" on web / announcement on native, failures on rows = showAlert; (4) role/aria-* props only; every in-page heading has an explicit aria-level of 2 (a level-less heading renders as a second h1 on web and could steal route focus). iOS speech below is expected from source reading and must be confirmed on a device.

TAB BAR / NAV
- iOS tab bar: four tabs; VoiceOver "Settings, tab, 4 of 4" (route removed, not hidden).
- Web: nav "Primary" has exactly four links Home, My Closet, Outfits, Settings; Settings has aria-current="page" on /settings, /settings/logs, /settings/tags.

HEADERS (all three settings screens)
- Title: web role="heading" aria-level=1 (react-navigation HeaderTitle), exactly one visible h1 per screen: "Settings", "Logs", "Edit tags". iOS: navigation bar title with header trait.
- Back control on Logs and Edit tags (default native-stack control, same as /closet/new): web <a role="link"> named "Settings, back", Enter activates; iOS "Settings, back button", two-finger scrub pops; Android "Navigate up" plus system back.
- After push: web focus on the new h1 (announces "Logs" / "Edit tags", heading level 1); iOS VoiceOver moves to the new screen (back button, then title).
- After back (control, gesture or browser back): web focus on h1 "Settings" (app-wide convention, not the originating row); iOS VoiceOver lands at the top of Settings.
- Unfocused screens leave the accessibility tree: settings/index keeps aria-hidden={!isFocused}; on web the stack and TabScene apply display:none.

SETTINGS INDEX
- Card heading "Closet": role="heading" aria-level={2}.
- "Edit tags": Pressable role="button" aria-label="Edit tags" (explicit so iOS does not append the chevron glyph); chevron Text aria-hidden. Web: <button>, Enter/Space activate. VoiceOver: "Edit tags, button". Activation -> /settings/tags.
- "Logs": Pressable role="button" aria-label="Logs"; same structure. VoiceOver: "Logs, button". Activation -> /settings/logs.
- Unchanged: radiogroup "Theme" with three radios, "Sign out" button.

LOGS
- Loading: wrapper role="progressbar" aria-label="Loading activity" (accessible on native); inner spinner aria-hidden. VoiceOver: "Loading activity".
- Error and no-closet texts: role="alert" (web announces on insert); load errors are also sent through announceForScreenReader on native.
- Empty: plain text "No activity yet."
- h2 "Recent activity in <closet name>": role="heading" aria-level={2}.
- List: View role="list" aria-label="Recent activity"; each entry View role="listitem" containing one Text (description, newline, nested timestamp Text) -> one VoiceOver stop per entry, read as "Ava created outfit Sunday Brunch, <date and time>"; web: one listitem per entry. No interactive elements, so nothing can lose focus when the list refreshes.

EDIT TAGS
- Loading: role="progressbar" aria-label="Loading tags".
- Load error: Text role="alert"; button "Try again" (role="button", name from text). After a successful retry the button is gone, so on web focus is moved to the "Add a tag" heading (focusOnWeb); native needs nothing.
- Section headings "Add a tag" and "Your tags": role="heading" aria-level={2}.
- Text field: TextInput aria-label="New tag"; visible label "New tag" above it. Web only (spread from a Record<string, string | boolean> like ariaCurrentPage in HeaderNav.web.tsx:27-29): aria-describedby = "new-tag-error new-tag-hint" when there is an error, else "new-tag-hint"; aria-invalid="true" only while an error is shown. Native: accessibilityHint="Up to 30 characters". VoiceOver: "New tag, text field, Up to 30 characters". Enter (web) / Done (iOS) submits and keeps focus in the field.
- Validation error: <Text id="new-tag-error" role="alert" key={nonce}>. The key remounts the node on every failed attempt so an identical message is announced again on web. Web: focus moves to (or stays in) the field, which then reads its name plus the error and hint. Native: announceForScreenReader(message); VoiceOver focus stays where it was (Add button or field). The error is cleared on the next keystroke and on a successful add. It is text, not colour alone.
- "Add tag" button: Pressable role="button", accessible name = visible text "Add tag" and it never changes; aria-busy={adding}; never disabled (a disabled web <button> drops focus to <body>, react-native-web Pressable/index.js:118-133); presses while busy are ignored. On success: field cleared, new row appended at the end of the list, focus unchanged (button or field), toast "Added tag <name>" spoken.
- Count sentence and removal note: plain text, read in order after the "Your tags" heading; not live regions (the toast already speaks each change).
- List: View role="list" aria-label="Your tags"; each row View role="listitem" (not `accessible`, so both children are reachable).
  - Name text. Active: "<name>". Removed: "<name> (removed)" - the state is in the words, the strike-through is decoration.
  - Row button, active state: role="button", aria-label={`Remove tag ${name}`}, visible "Remove" (visible word is contained in the name). VoiceOver: "Remove tag Casual, button".
  - Row button, removed state: same element, aria-label={`Undo remove tag ${name}`}, visible "Undo". VoiceOver: "Undo remove tag Casual, button".
  - In flight: aria-busy true, name and visible text unchanged, opacity 0.6, extra presses ignored; never disabled, never unmounted.
  - Remove success: focus stays on the same button (now Undo); toast "Removed tag <name>. Undo is available." is spoken. Activating again undoes; toast "Restored tag <name>"; the button is Remove again; focus still on it.
  - Failure: showAlert("Couldn't remove tag" | "Couldn't restore tag", message) - UIAlertController on iOS (VoiceOver reads title, message, OK), window.alert on web; when dismissed, focus returns to the same row button, which still exists.
- There is no confirm dialog and no window.confirm anywhere in the flow.
- Stylist mode / no closet: the same screen; ownership sentence or the no-closet paragraph is ordinary text directly after the title.

CREATE OUTFIT
- With tags: field label "Tag"; iOS button "Tag, required", value "Not selected" or the tag, opening the native action sheet; web <select aria-label="Tag" aria-required="true"> listing tags verbatim. If the chosen tag is removed while the form is open the select returns to "Select a tag" and Save disables as it does today.
- Without tags: one sentence of text in place of the select (copy in uiSpec); Save is enabled once name, description and an item are present.

OUTFITS FILTER

If the client ships first, selectWithLabelsFallback keeps closets loading with the ten defaults and add/remove fail with 'Editing tags is not available yet. Please try again later.' That fallback relies on PostgREST reporting Postgres code 42703 for the missing column (also inside the closets(...) embed) and PGRST202 for a missing function; neither was exercised here. Nothing was built or run: the SQL is correct by inspection only (array slicing for target_position, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE under RLS, the [[:cntrl:]] regex and the IMMUTABLE validator inside a CHECK should be exercised in PGlite or a local Supabase before production).

The design avoids programmatic VoiceOver focus and alert-dismissal timing precisely because they cannot be tested here.

Toast now queues its announcement on iOS for every screen that toasts (voice notes, item/outfit updated, background removal, join closet). This matches the existing RemoveBackgroundButton pattern but is a global behaviour change that only a device can confirm.

Tag lists reach other sessions lazily: a stylist's running session, or the owner's second device, keeps its copy until closet mode is toggled or the app restarts (ClosetContext only refetches then, src/context/ClosetContext.tsx:51-97). A stale list is harmless (an outfit may be saved with a tag the owner just removed and then shows only under All) but is not live.

Removed tags stay on existing outfits, and already-installed iOS builds keep offering the hardcoded ten and writing them to outfits.labels regardless of the owner's list. The app must keep tolerating outfit labels that are in no list. Matching is exact and case-sensitive, so removing 'Work' and later typing 'work' does not reconnect old outfits; only Undo (same string) or retyping the identical spelling does.
Undo exists only until the Edit tags screen next gains focus; after that a removed tag must be retyped. There is no 'Restore default tags' button by decision.

strengths: SQL runs as written on the stubbed schema (same throwaway Postgres 16). Backfill gave the existing closet ten rows with sort_order 1..10; a closet inserted as an authenticated user was seeded with ten by the trigger; the owner's 'work' raised 23505; ' x', 'a  b', a tab and 31 characters raised 23514; a stylist insert raised the RLS error (42501) and a stylist delete touched 0 rows; an owner UPDATE touched 0 rows; an outsider saw 0 rows; deleting the closet cascaded.
Only design where every invariant (length, whitespace, case-insensitive uniqueness, owner-only writes) holds for any client, with no UPDATE path on closets at all.
Only design that keeps Outfits and Create outfit working if the client ships before the migration (falls back to the ten defaults).
Stylists get fresh tag lists (refetch on focus, keyed by closet id), and Edit tags always edits the user's own closet regardless of closet mode.
Reserves the name 'All', matches case-insensitively, re-checks the tag before save, keeps /about working through a withAnchor redirect and adds /settings deep links.

Inline role=alert validation with aria-invalid/aria-describedby on web (react-native-web forwards both: node_modules/react-native-web/dist/modules/forwardedProps/index.js) and an explicit announcement on native. Logs keeps the previous entries instead of flashing a spinner on refocus.

defects.where: uiSpec F handleRemove versus a11ySpec section 5 'After removal'
defects.problem: The announcement and the focus move are ordered so the announcement is cut off on iOS. handleRemove calls showToast right after removeLabel resolves, but the VoiceOver focus move is deferred 500 ms. The focus-change speech then interrupts the queued 'Removed tag X'. The a11ySpec claims the opposite order.
defects.evidence: Design text: 'await removeLabel(label); showToast(...)' and 'iOS/Android -> setTimeout(() => AccessibilityInfo.sendAccessibilityEvent(node, 'focus'), 500)'. /home/user/Zeeba/src/components/RemoveBackgroundButton.tsx:162-172 documents that focus speech cuts announcements off.
defects.fix: Fire the toast from the same delayed callback, after the focus move (minimal design's order), or adopt the a11y design's no-focus-move Remove/Undo row.

defects.where: a11ySpec section 5 (confirm alert, then 500 ms timer, then sendAccessibilityEvent)
defects.problem: VoiceOver correctness depends on an untestable magic delay after UIAlertController dismissal. If UIKit's own refocus lands later than 500 ms (slow device, Reduce Motion off), focus returns to an unmounted button and the cursor is lost. The user's explicit requirement is that VoiceOver works, and no iPhone is available.
defects.evidence: Design text: 'The delay lets UIKit finish returning VoiceOver focus after the alert closes; tune on a device.' No existing use of sendAccessibilityEvent in /home/user/Zeeba/src.
defects.fix: Do not unmount the focused control: keep the row and flip the button to Undo (a11y design).

defects.problem: useEffect(() => { seq.current = {}; setEntries({}) }, [dataService, userId]) runs after child focus effects in the same commit. A refresh that a consumer started in that commit has its ticket wiped, so its result is discarded and labels stay null until the next focus (Create outfit shows a spinner with Save disabled).
defects.evidence: Design text: refresh stores 'only if seq.current[closetId] === ticket'. React runs child effects before parent effects. /home/user/Zeeba/src/context/ClosetContext.tsx:52 keeps a stale myCloset across sign-out, so a closet id can be present at the moment userId changes.
defects.fix: Key the store by identity (state {identity, entries}, derived on read) instead of resetting in an effect, or bump a generation counter that tickets include.

defects.problem: The spec puts a network await before submitting is set ('before setSubmitting's try block'). Save stays enabled during the round trip, so a double tap can create two outfits.
defects.evidence: /home/user/Zeeba/src/components/CreateOutfitForm.tsx:168-169 and :184: canSubmit depends on submitting, which today is set synchronously before the first await.
defects.fix: Call setSubmitting(true) before the refresh and clear it on the early return.

defects.where: dataLayerSpec section 9 (fallback to DEFAULT_OUTFIT_LABELS on load error, 'no error is shown')
defects.problem: A transient network failure silently swaps a closet's custom list for the ten defaults in the filter row and the Tag select. An outfit can then be saved with a tag the owner removed, with nothing telling a screen-reader user the list is not theirs.
defects.evidence: Design text: 'tagNames = labels ? ... : labelsError ? DEFAULT_OUTFIT_LABELS : null' and 'If the tag list fails to load, the ten defaults are offered (no error is shown)'.
defects.fix: Use the fallback only for the missing-table error (42P01 or PGRST205). For other errors keep the last good list, or show a retry.

defects.problem: Same as the minimal design: aria-label on ActivityIndicator is not spoken on iOS.
defects.evidence: /home/user/Zeeba/node_modules/react-native/Libraries/Components/ActivityIndicator/ActivityIndicator.js:96-104.
defects.fix: Use the a11y design's LoadingIndicator wrapper.

defects.problem: When a closet's outfits carry both 'vintage' and 'Vintage', which spelling is kept depends on database collation, not on the data. Check (8) expects 'vintage'; my run kept 'Vintage'.
defects.evidence: Executed with outfits {vintage,Work} and {Vintage,' padded ',All}: the rows added were 'Vintage' and 'padded' (SELECT DISTINCT ... ORDER BY 1, 2 with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING).
defects.fix: Harmless because matching is case-insensitive; correct the expectation, or pick the most-used spelling.

defects.where: overall surface (new table, two SECURITY DEFINER triggers, new provider, new service, per-focus fetches)
defects.problem: The largest change set for an owner-only add/remove list. Outfits and Create outfit gain a request and a loading state (the pill row pops in after load) that the column designs avoid.
defects.evidence: filesToTouch lists 25 entries including OutfitLabelsContext.tsx and supabaseOutfitLabelsService.ts. previewService delays each call 400 ms (/home/user/Zeeba/src/services/previewService.ts:26,34-36).
defects.fix: If the table is kept, render pills from the last known list immediately. Otherwise take the column plus CHECK plus RPC storage and keep only the refresh-on-focus idea.

strengths: SQL runs as written on the stubbed schema (same throwaway Postgres 16). ADD COLUMN backfilled both closets with ten; a new closet got ten; target_position 3, 1, 999 and 0 inserted and clamped correctly; adding into '{}' worked; 'casual ' raised the duplicate message; remove was idempotent; stylist and anon got 'Only the closet owner can edit its tags.'

The CHECK validator closes the direct-PATCH hole the minimal design leaves open: array['a','A'], array[NULL], a tab and a 31-element array were all rejected with closets_outfit_labels_valid, while '{}' was accepted.

Remove/Undo in place: the focused button never unmounts and nothing is disabled, so there is no confirm dialog, no window.confirm, no programmatic VoiceOver focus and no alert-dismissal timing. It is the only remove flow whose iOS behaviour does not depend on untestable assumptions.
LoadingIndicator wrapper correctly handles the native ActivityIndicator not mapping aria-label (ActivityIndicator.js:96-104).

Client-first deploy keeps closets loading (42703 fallback to defaults, PGRST202 mapped to a message). Edit tags always edits the user's own closet. The Tag field renders only when activeClosetId is set. /about keeps working through a withAnchor redirect with no native config change.

Inline role=alert validation with key={nonce} so a repeated identical error re-announces on web; aria-invalid/aria-describedby on web and accessibilityHint plus a queued announcement on native. Concrete Playwright acceptance checks are listed.

Removing 'Date Night' and later typing 'Date night' gives a pill that matches none of the old outfits, and 'Date Night' cannot be added back while 'Date night' exists. No autoCapitalize is specified on the input, so iOS sentence-case makes this likely. Outfits cannot be re-tagged either.

crossCuttingMisses: No design gives a way to tag or re-tag an existing outfit, yet all three allow emptying the list and removing tags. An outfit created while the list is empty, or whose tag was removed, can never be filtered again: /home/user/Zeeba/src/services/dataService.types.ts:323-326 (UpdateOutfitInput is name and description only) and /home/user/Zeeba/src/components/EditOutfitForm.tsx has no tag field. All three list this as out of scope; it should be put to the user as a product decision.

No normaliser strips zero-width or format characters (U+200B to U+200D, U+2060). JavaScript trim() and \s do not match U+200B, so the client check passes; a visually blank tag would show as an empty pill and a button VoiceOver reads as 'Remove tag' with no name. I could not confirm the database side (the test cluster was SQL_ASCII).

The Settings tab keeps its nested stack state and no design sets popToTopOnBlur. Leave Logs or Edit tags open, switch tabs, tap Settings: VoiceOver says 'Settings, tab' and the user lands on Logs. The web 'Settings' nav link from /settings/logs pushes a second index (same as /closet/new today). All three note it under risks but none fixes it.

Already-installed native builds keep the hardcoded ten tags and the Logs tab. They will keep writing removed tags to outfits.labels and will never show custom tags. All three accept this; the user should be told it ends only when the new build is installed.
No design can verify native iOS VoiceOver. The minimal and robust remove flows add programmatic focus moves that cannot be tested here; only the a11y design avoids depending on that.
The Toast change (queued announcement on iOS, /home/user/Zeeba/src/components/Toast.tsx:27-29) is shared by all three and changes every toast in the app. None scopes it or adds a way to opt out.

The Toast Text is always mounted with role=alert at opacity 0 (Toast.tsx:44-52), so on iOS VoiceOver can still swipe onto an invisible stale 'Removed tag X' after it fades. Pre-existing, but all three lean on the toast for the tag flows and none clears the message.

critique.recommendedBase:
Build on the a11y design (design 3).

- **VoiceOver:** it is the only one whose remove flow needs no programmatic focus move and no alert-dismissal timing. The button stays mounted and flips between Remove and Undo. Given that VoiceOver must work and no iPhone is available, that matters most.
- **Storage:** column plus invoker RPCs plus an IMMUTABLE validator CHECK. I ran the migration on a throwaway Postgres 16 with the baseline policies stubbed and it behaved as specified, including rejecting junk arrays that the minimal design accepts.
- **Deploy order:** closets keep loading if the client ships before the migration.
- **Scope:** Edit tags always edits the user's own closet, the labelled-spinner wrapper is correct for iOS, and /about keeps working.

Its real weaknesses are case-sensitive matching, effect-based selection resets, stale labels for stylists, and the retry focus drop. All are cheap to fix with ideas from the other two.

- **Minimal design:** not a safe base as written. A client-first deploy takes down closet loading, and it makes Edit tags read-only in stylist mode.
- **Robust design:** the strongest data model, but the largest surface (table, two triggers, new provider, per-focus fetches). Its iOS remove flow fires the toast before a 500 ms delayed focus move, so the announcement would be cut off.

All three migrations were run only against stubs on PG16 with SQL_ASCII. Still unverified: PG17 and Unicode cases, the PostgREST error codes the fallback relies on, and anything on a real iPhone.
ideasToGraft: From minimal: derive the effective selection during render instead of resetting it in an effect. In OutfitsGrid, activeLabel = selected && labels.includes(selected) ? selected : null; the same for CreateOutfitForm selectedLabel. No stale frame, and the choice survives Remove then Undo.
From minimal and robust: match outfits to tags case-insensitively on a trimmed, lower-cased key (robust's outfitLabelKey), and set autoCapitalize="words" on the New tag input.
From robust: reserve the name 'All' (any case) in the client validator, the add RPC and the validator function, so the filter row never has two tabs named All.
From robust: turn control characters into spaces in normalizeOutfitLabel and in the RPC before validating, so the CHECK never surfaces a raw constraint error.

From robust: refresh the active closet's labels when Outfits and Create outfit gain focus (a small getClosetOutfitLabels(closetId) read of closets.outfit_labels pushed through applyClosetLabels), so stylists and second devices see the owner's edits. Guard applyClosetLabels against older in-flight context loads with a sequence counter.
From robust: Logs keeps the previously loaded entries for the same closet instead of clearing to a spinner on every focus, and shows a caption naming the closet.
From robust: remove textTransform 'capitalize' from /home/user/Zeeba/src/components/NativeSelect.tsx:164 as well as FilterPills.tsx:118, so Android shows tags verbatim.
From robust (optional): the pre-save tag re-check in CreateOutfitForm with the 'Tag no longer available' alert. Set submitting before the await.
From robust (optional): add '/settings' and '/settings/*' to the AASA file and an Android pathPrefix '/settings' if Logs and Edit tags should open in the app from links. It needs a native rebuild.
From minimal: order any focus move before the toast. This applies to the a11y design's one focus move (focusOnWeb after a retry) and anywhere else focus is moved.

From minimal (optional): the Cloudflare line '/about /settings/logs 301' in /home/user/Zeeba/public/_redirects alongside the in-app redirect route, and correct the '/about.html' example in that file's comment at line 14.
Fix within the a11y design: keep the 'Try again' button mounted (aria-busy) while retrying, and make Undo and add-by-typing converge on server order after each mutation.
For all: before merge, run the chosen migration and the 42703/PGRST202 fallback against a local Supabase (PG17, UTF-8), including a zero-width-character tag and a client-before-migration smoke test.
